commit.message:
fix: install the merge-block hook again, and fail closed when it cannot be

The PreToolUse hook that denies `gh pr merge`, `gh api PUT .../pulls/N/merge` and the
`curl` equivalent has not been installed on any fresh state dir since the 2026-08-09
Python conversion. `lifecycle.preflight` resolved its two assets as
`Path(__file__).parent / ...` while they sat in repo-root `driver/`, so the
`if template.is_file():` guard skipped the render, nothing was written, and
`invoke_agent` went on passing `--settings <path that was never written>`.

It looked fine locally because `.driver-state/settings.json` is an Aug 6
pre-conversion leftover that happens to point at a real script. The decafclaw state
dir's copy points into a worktree that no longer exists.

Three things, in the order they matter:

1. The assets move into `src/agent_sessions/driver/`, beside the module that loads
   them. Verified the wheel ships them (hatch already includes non-Python files under
   the package). `driver/` now holds exactly the compatibility launcher, which is the
   coherent end state of the conversion.

2. The render fails closed. `render_hook_settings` dies on a missing, non-executable
   or unreadable asset instead of skipping. A safety control that silently omits
   itself when its asset is absent is worse than one that is missing, because nothing
   reports the difference -- that is the whole reason this survived.

3. The tests grade the code instead of the artifact. The three previous tests never
   touched the install path: one asserted a string appeared in `lifecycle.py`'s source
   text, one loaded the template by repo-relative literal and checked its shape, and
   one shelled out to `jq` to redo the substitution and asserted that jq works. They
   all passed throughout. Replaced with tests that call `preflight` and assert the
   rendered file exists, targets Bash, and names an executable that exists -- plus a
   control proving a missing template now stops the run.

`backend_permission_probe` no longer re-implements the substitution; it delegates to
`render_hook_settings`. Its own copy was the only correct resolver while the driver's
was wrong, so the probe attested to a hook no real run installed.

Also adds `git push -f` to both backends' deny lists -- the short form matched
nothing, since only `git push --force` was spelled out. Deliberately *not* adding
tool-level rules for the REST merge paths: those patterns would have to match
mid-command, `--help` does not state whether the rule syntax supports that, and an
unverified entry in a floor whose value is that it is verified is the wrong trade.
The hook covers them, now per-vector tested, and `make backend-permission-probe` is
the one live run that would settle the syntax question.

Updates the claims this move falsified: the `driver/**` allowlist clause in both
governance files now says plainly that it grants nothing, and `orientation.md`'s
layout bullets and file table point at the real locations. Its prose restatement of
the allowlist is deleted rather than corrected -- it had already drifted by omitting
`tests/**`, which is what the no-duplicate-live-sources rule exists to prevent.

Refs #261 (S1, S2, part of D3, H4).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: stop the suites writing into the operator's home directory

There was no conftest.py anywhere in the repo, so nothing pinned XDG_STATE_HOME.
`lifecycle.preflight` derives its state dir from that variable (falling back to
$HOME/.local/state) plus `agent-session/<repo-with-dashes>`, and the fixture repo is
`owner/repo` -- so every test that drove the driver without passing --state-dir wrote
to a real path in $HOME. Measured before this change:

    ~/.local/state/agent-session/owner-repo/   897 run dirs, 1748 ledger rows, 11M
                                               plus inbox.md, parked.jsonl, workspaces/

still growing, with rows timestamped during this session's own test runs.

The worst consequence is not disk. `make evidence` reads a per-repo runs.jsonl, and
the fix for it currently reading a superseded archive is to point it at the live state
root -- at which point 1748 fabricated rows become "evidence" about runs that never
happened. So this has to land first.

An autouse fixture in the new tests/conftest.py pins the variable per test.
tests/driver/test_state_isolation.py is its control: it drives preflight with no
--state-dir and asserts the result lands inside tmp_path, plus a polarity case that
unsets the pin and confirms the fallback still resolves to the path that leaked.
Without the control this would be an assertion about the suite rather than a check on
it, which is how the original went unnoticed.

Verified: a full `make check` now leaves both counts at 897/1748, unchanged.

Second fixture, for the lock global. The full-loop harness had:

    monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE", None)
    # ... so no pass can leave a live lock behind

which did nothing -- that module binds a copy of the value at import while `locks`
mutates its own global through `global`, and nothing in src/ reads the re-exported
name. The symptom was visible on every single run: real `Releasing lock for #N...`
lines at pytest exit, the atexit hook firing after monkeypatch had restored the true
subprocess.run. Survivable only because the tmp_path repos have no `origin` to receive
a ref deletion.

Patched on the owning module, plus an autouse teardown that clears it.

Worth recording that the teardown started as an assertion that the global was already
None, and it failed at once on the full-loop passes -- correctly, because a pass that
acquires a lock and returns really does end holding it. That is the driver's designed
behaviour: the lock covers the process. Asserting against it would have been asserting
that the driver releases something it is built to keep, so the fixture resets and does
not assert. The reset is the part that removes the harm.

Refs #261 (C3, C4).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: point make evidence at the live run ledgers

`evidence.py` hardcoded `Path(".driver-state")`, which #27 superseded. The driver writes
to ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/agent-session/<repo-with-dashes>/, so the report
rendered a cold archive: 38 rows, last written 2026-08-06, none carrying the `phase`
field that is the report's primary grouping key -- which is why every PHASE cell printed
`unknown`.

That is worse than an ordinary stale path. `docs_check.check_world_state_claims` fails
any bare count in the docs with "use `make evidence` instead", and design.md and
orientation.md both cite this command as the only authoritative source for what has
actually run. The doc-rot detector's prescribed remedy was reporting dead data.

Discovery now defaults to every per-repo ledger under the live state root, with
--state-dir and --repo to narrow it. The derivation is imported from
`run_progress.default_state_dir` rather than reimplemented; a third copy of that
expression is how the second one went wrong. Unparsed lines are counted and reported
instead of silently dropped -- a partial final line is normal, but a report that quietly
loses rows cannot be told apart from one with fewer runs to report.

Now prints 319 real runs across both repos with real phase names.

This had to land *after* the test-isolation fix in the previous commit. The live state
root held ~1748 fabricated `owner/repo` rows from the suites; repointing first would have
laundered fixture data into the report. Those rows are now gone and the ledgers are real.

Tests rewritten against real files in tmp_path. The old one replaced `builtins.open`
process-wide and forced `Path.is_file` to return True, so every read in the call window
got the fixture and the discovery path was never exercised -- which is precisely how a
hardcoded `.driver-state` survived #27. Includes a polarity check that a
`.driver-state/runs.jsonl` in the working directory is *not* picked up.

Makefile, same subject:
- `evidence` was missing from .PHONY -- the only omission -- and from `help`, despite
  CLAUDE.md telling readers twice to cite it. Also adds the missing `doctor-self` and
  `watch-self` lines.
- `docs-check`'s rationale comment had drifted onto `evidence`: the recipe was inserted
  between the comment and the target it explains, leaving docs-check reading as
  unjustified. Reattached, and `evidence` given its own.
- Drops `driver-test-sh` from .PHONY. It had no rule anywhere in the file, so it existed
  in make's target database only because .PHONY named it, and `make driver-test-sh`
  exited 0 having done nothing.

Also corrects `run_progress.default_state_dir`'s docstring, which cited
`agent-session-driver.sh:347` -- a file the conversion left eight lines long.

Refs #261 (C2, H6, part of H10, part of T4, part of X5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: narrow every label_manager remove list, and stop failures reading as "no labels"

`removable()` exists because `gh issue edit --remove-label X` errors when the *repo*
has no label X at all -- not just when the issue lacks it -- and a fresh target repo
only has the labels something already created, so the whole edit fails, add included.
It was applied to park, unpark and clear-attempts. `spec`, `attempt` and `merge-ready`
kept building their remove lists unconditionally.

Two of the three are on paths the driver takes on every run, and both swallow the
failure:

    parking.py:82   increment_attempts -> `attempt --count N`   except Exception: pass
    parking.py:369  apply_park_state   -> `merge-ready`         except Exception: pass

So on a fresh target repo the attempt counter silently never increments -- and the
attempt counter is the thing that stops a phase looping forever -- while the
gate-eligible success path silently fails to stamp merge-ready.

The test file's own header diagnosed this in full ("There were no tests here at all
before this file, which is why three commands carried the same bug") and then covered
only the three commands that got the fix. Eight new tests, written against the existing
FakeGh, fail with the exact production error before the change.

Second half, in scope because the first half widened its reach.
`get_current_labels` did `except Exception: return []`, making a rate limit, a 401 and a
genuinely unlabelled issue indistinguishable -- while every caller reads the result as
fact. `validate_transition` derives `is_parked` from it, so an empty list means "not
parked" and the guard permits re-speccing or re-attempting a parked issue. And now that
all six commands narrow through `removable`, an empty list would also silently skip
removals. Both are a null rendering as a positive.

It now propagates, and `main` catches it before touching anything: exit 1, a message
naming the issue, and no edit attempted. The driver's callers already wrap these in
`except Exception`, so they degrade to a no-op rather than a wrong action.

`ensure_label_exists` likewise narrowed from a bare `except RuntimeError: pass` to the
already-exists case, so a 403 from a read-only token no longer looks like success.

Refs #261 (C1, C9).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: correct usage.md's operator-facing claims

Six defects, all verified against the code. These matter more than ordinary doc rot
because usage.md is what someone reads while a run is misbehaving.

**The park label was wrong, and the doc told you to act on it.** It named
`driver-parked` three times; the label is `agent-session:needs-human`, renamed by Epic
#145. `driver-parked` appears nowhere in src/ -- it survives only in the session that
proposed it. And the sentence carrying the wrong name is the one instructing the manual
recovery ("you take the label off by hand"), so it was the wrong string most likely to be
used. The second park label, `agent-session:needs-human-interactive`, was undocumented
and is equally load-bearing: selection treats either as parked.

**The Outcomes table had two of nine rows inverted.** It said `gate-human` does not park
and `incomplete` does. `apply_park_state` calls `park_label_add` for `gate-human` and
`park_label_remove` for `incomplete`, whose own log line reads "leaving unparked so the
loop can re-evaluate later". An operator reading the old table would wait for the loop to
re-pick a `gate-human` issue -- it never will -- and hand-unpark an `incomplete` one that
was already unparked. Now lists which outcomes add the label, which remove it, and that
`gate-eligible` adds `merge-ready` instead, with a pointer to the function as authority.

**"runs `express` on them unattended"** -- `express` appears nowhere in lifecycle.py. The
driver runs one phase per invocation from an eight-phase set, and `request_review` runs
with no agent at all. Part 4's whole "one run = one express pass" framing followed from
this; the ladder is what the outcomes and attempt counters are in service of.

**"What eligible means" described a superseded algorithm, including one inverted
condition.** It said the board column is "advisory -- reported but doesn't gate", while
`router.select` filters to issues on the board with status `Ready` (or board priority
P0/P1) or carrying a P0-P5 label unless --all-issues. That inversion is the most likely
cause of a "why is my queue dry" investigation. It also missed that an open PR is now the
*highest* priority rather than an exclusion, that `needs-review` is selectable and routes
to `refine`, and that eligibility reads a label as well as the body marker. Replaced with
the actual ladder, plus the exclusions and the `MAX_PHASE_ATTEMPTS` park reason an
operator will see in the output. Records that P4 Escalate is declared and never populated.

**The credential table contradicted its own next section.** The table said the write
token lives in "your shell, never `.env`"; the prose 25 lines below says both go in
`.env` and dates the decision to 2026-08-10. `.env.example` and `credentials.py` side
with the prose.

**GitHub App auth is implemented and was documented as not built.** "There is no third
option short of a GitHub App" and "None of these is built" -- while `credentials.py`
implements the whole path: three variables plus `GH_APP_*` aliases, `generate_app_jwt`,
`fetch_app_installation_token`, minting scoped read and write installation tokens
separately. It is also the answer to the fine-grained-PAT resource-owner limit the same
section describes as a dead end. Documented, along with `DRIVER_GH_BOARD_TOKEN`, and both
added to `.env.example` -- with the warning that the key belongs outside the repository,
since that is exactly where one was found.

**The per-run artifact table listed a file that is never written** (`denials.txt` -- no
such artifact exists anywhere in src/) and omitted three that are: `stderr.txt`, the
first thing to read on a driver-fault; `parsed.json`; and `inbox.md`, which is the human
work queue every escalation appends to and had no mention in the guide at all.

Also corrects design.md's park-label decision line to keep the decision and note the
rename, rather than leaving a name that shipped and then changed.

Refs #261 (D1, part of D2).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: repair the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md divergence, and delete the regrown roadmap table

`diff CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md` had four hunks. The risk-gated section -- the only part
`docs_check.check_risk_policy_parity` guards -- was byte-identical, so the guard was
working. Everything outside it had drifted, which is the whole argument.

Hunks 1-3 were a find-and-replace applied to things that are not harness-relative:

- `~/.claude/skills/` had become `~/.Codex/skills/` in AGENTS.md. That is a *filesystem
  path*; it does not change based on who is reading the file. It resolved on this machine
  only because APFS is case-insensitive, and the capitalisation matches no real directory.
- The same substitution hit the reference-skill path, and there both directories genuinely
  exist as separate copies -- so "adapt from it; don't edit it" named two different
  sources of truth depending on which file an agent had read.
- `claude -p` had become `Codex -p`. Worth being precise about why that is bad: `codex`
  *does* accept `-p`, but it is `--profile <CONFIG_PROFILE_V2>`. So the line would not
  have errored; it would have silently consumed the next token as a config profile name.
  Non-interactive Codex is `codex exec`.

All three are now phrased so they are true for either reader: the skills directories are
named as a set, the reference skill is described as installed per harness, and the
headless invocation lists both CLIs.

Hunk 4 was real content drift, one-directional -- AGENTS.md was the older text. It omitted
the "a world-state claim can be phrased as a judgment" rule entirely, understated
docs-check by one of its six checks, and carried "two real defects... two readings", the
exact undated-count pattern the rule two lines above forbids. Synced from CLAUDE.md.

The two files are now byte-identical, which sharpens rather than settles the structural
question: whether AGENTS.md should simply point at CLAUDE.md. That change needs
`docs_check.check_risk_policy_parity` taught about the pointer shape, and it is a call
about whether a Codex-hosted run needs its instruction file to stand alone. Left for a
human; recorded in #261 (G1).

Separately, design.md's roadmap table is deleted. The section opens "The backlog is not
maintained here any more" and then reproduced eight rows, of which seven were closed
issues. CLAUDE.md cites this exact section as its precedent for not duplicating a live
source in prose, and the table grew back anyway. Replaced with the `gh issue list` query.

Refs #261 (G1 partial, D2).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor: give the driver's output and clock a home, breaking the barrel cycle

`agent_session_driver.py` was a 143-line re-export barrel that defined nothing, and the
package reached back through it constantly: 14 function-local imports across `lifecycle`,
`board`, `parking` and `locks`, existing purely to break the cycle the barrel created.

Two distinct things were tangled in there.

**Five spellings of one output helper set.** `say` defined four times, `log` twice, `die`
twice. Three were byte-identical; `board`'s three were trampolines that went through the
barrel to arrive at `lifecycle`'s copies. Writing one line to stdout could take three hops
through an import cycle, and which implementation you got depended on which module you
were in.

**The barrel was also the clock**, and this is the part worth stating plainly, because it
is easy to mistake for a vestige: eight call sites across five modules read
`agent_session_driver.datetime`, not because they wanted the barrel but because patching
that single attribute freezes time everywhere at once. The full-loop suite depends on it
for byte-stable `runs.jsonl` rows. That is a real and useful seam -- it was just housed in
a module whose only job was re-exporting, so every module that needed the clock had to
import the barrel from inside a function body.

New `output.py`: `say`, `log`, `die`, and `now()` as the named clock. It imports nothing
from `agent_sessions.driver`, which is what lets everything else import it at module
scope. All eight clock reads and all five output-helper definitions now route through it.

Result: function-local barrel imports drop from 14 across four modules to 7 across two --
`board.py` and `locks.py` are out of the cycle entirely. The barrel no longer re-exports

refactor: import the output helpers instead of re-exporting them

Les caught this on review: `say = output.say` with a comment saying it exists
"because `agent_session_driver` and the tests import them from this module". He
asked whether that implies fixing the importers instead. It does, and the comment
was partly false.

Measured:

- **No test imports them from anywhere.** That half of the justification was
  invented. `test_driver.py` in fact documents the opposite — it patches
  `board.log` directly, with a comment explaining that patching a re-export
  "no longer reaches it, the same shape as the CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE patch that
  silently did nothing."
- **The facade did import them, from `lifecycle`**, and re-exported them in
  `__all__`, and **nothing anywhere consumed the result.** So the alias existed to
  feed a re-export that fed nobody.
- **`pr_checks.py` aliased `say` and never called it.** Purely dead.

So the chain was `output.say` -> alias in `lifecycle` -> facade imports it *from
lifecycle* -> `__all__` -> no consumer.

What it bought was a trap. A re-export of a function is a bound copy, so
`monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "log", ...)` reads as patching the
emitter and patches nothing — which is precisely the `CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` defect
this branch fixes two commits earlier. Leaving `say`/`log`/`die` on the facade set
the same trap for the next person.

Now:

- `board`, `lifecycle` and `parking` bind them with a real
  `from agent_sessions.driver.output import ...`. Same brevity — `lifecycle` calls
  `say` 55 times — and `lifecycle.say` stays patchable the way the suites already
  patch `board.log`. It just no longer pretends to be a re-export.
- `pr_checks` drops the dead alias.
- The facade stops importing and exporting them, and its docstring says why.

**The clock is deliberately different.** `output.now()` stays a module-qualified
call everywhere, because a bound copy could not be frozen, and freezing it is how
the suites get deterministic timestamps. That asymmetry is now stated where it
could otherwise look like an inconsistency.

A guard pins it: nothing may put `say`/`log`/`die` back into the facade's `__all__`.
Mutation-tested — adding one back fails it. Worth asserting because the re-export is
one line and reads as harmless.

fix(#261): populate the venv before make check fans out

`make check` failed on a cold .venv, deterministically:

    $ rm -rf .venv && make check
    error: Failed to install: ruff-0.16.2-py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl
    make[1]: *** [commit-lint] Error 2
    make: *** [check] Error 2

Seven jobs run under `$(MAKE) -j check-parallel` and every one of them enters
through `uv run`, which creates and populates .venv on demand. They race for it,
and one loses. Every fresh worktree hits this -- it is how the branch this lands
on was found, on its first `make check`.

What makes it worth more than a one-line fix is the shape of the failure. The
message names a wheel and an install, so it reads as a network fault or a broken
toolchain; nothing in it points at make parallelism. And the honest response --
rerun it -- succeeds, because the venv is warm by then. That trains the operator
to treat the project's only aggregate gate as flaky.

Fix: a `venv` target running `uv sync --quiet`, reached from `check`'s recipe
rather than as a prerequisite, so `make -j check` cannot reorder it.

Verified: `rm -rf .venv && make check` was exit 2 before and is exit 0 after.
The new frozen suite derives the plan from `make -n check` (which expands the
recursive sub-make) and asserts positionally that the first `uv` command sits
above the fan-out; it failed with the real diagnosis before this change. C2 is
the control -- it requires the fan-out to still be concurrent with more than one
`uv run` consumer, so C1 cannot pass by the race being refactored away silently.

New finding, not among the ones recorded on the issue.

fix(#261): make the recovery path record the row it says it recorded

N2, a finding X4's new coverage turned up, and Les's call on which half was wrong.

`run_classify_only` ended by printing "recorded to runs.jsonl. Nothing was
merged." Only `classify_and_record` ever opened `ctx.runs_log`. Park state *was*
applied -- so an operator recovering a dead run got the issue parked, a line
saying the ledger was written, and no row for the run that parked it. A hole in
the per-run provenance exactly where a run died, which is the case you most want
recorded, and the ledger `make evidence` and every world-state claim read.

Nothing had ever exercised `--classify-only`, which is why it survived.

Three parts:

**One row builder.** `append_run_row` is now the only place the ledger row's shape
is written, and both paths call it. The two had drifted far enough to disagree
about whether a run was recorded at all; #261's T3 names the pair as a live drift
risk, and a second hand-built copy would have re-created it on the spot.

**The inflight marker carries its phase.** `phase` is `evidence.py`'s primary
grouping key, so a recovered row without one is a run that happened and cannot be
counted -- the state the pre-#27 archive was in, and the reason every PHASE cell
used to render `unknown`. The marker is written at the start of every run and
exists to describe the run in flight, so the phase belongs in it. Markers written
before the field existed get a blank, not a crash and not a guess; that control is
asserted, because a `KeyError` here would turn the recovery path into a second
failure at the worst possible moment.

**`exit` is -1.** The run's own process never reported one, which is the situation
this path exists for. A recovered row saying `exit: 0` would be a fabrication.

Both sides of the marker coupling are asserted, in separate passes: that recovery
reads the phase, and that a normal run writes it. The producer is `invoke_agent`
and the consumer is `run_classify_only`, which is exactly the shape that goes
stale unnoticed.

The check this replaces asserted the *discrepancy* rather than either half, and
said so: "whichever way it is settled, this is the test that has to change, and
the diff will say which was chosen." It was settled in favour of recording.

Verified: all four checks failed before this change. `make check` green.

Tier: needs-review. `lifecycle.py` is gated, and this writes the provenance ledger.

docs(#261): make AGENTS.md a pointer, and teach the parity check that shape

G1. The two governance files were byte-identical, and
`check_risk_policy_parity` guarded only the `Risk-gated paths` section. That
section stayed in sync for its whole life. Everything outside it drifted, in three
ways worth naming because they are what a copy does:

- a find-and-replace rewrote a real filesystem path into one that exists nowhere,
  resolving on one machine only because its filesystem is case-insensitive;
- a second invented a `codex -p` flag meaning "print". `-p` is `--profile`, so it
  would not have errored -- it would have silently eaten the next argument;
- one section lost a rule from AGENTS.md alone, and the surviving copy was stale.

The guarded part held; the unguarded remainder did not. There is no bound on how
much unguarded remainder there will be, so AGENTS.md now has none.

**The check was taught the shape rather than relaxed**, and the two ways a pointer
can be wrong are what the new checks are about:

- a short file is not a pointer just by being short -- it has to name the
  instruction file it defers to;
- a pointer whose target has no policy is worthless. This is the failure that
  would otherwise be silent: delete CLAUDE.md's section and, with AGENTS.md
  reduced to a pointer, *neither* file has one, the parity check has nothing to
  compare, and it passes on an empty set. That is the null-as-positive shape this
  detector exists to catch, arriving inside the detector.

And the half-migrated case is explicitly not a pointer: a file that links CLAUDE.md
*and* keeps its own `## Risk-gated paths` section still has to match it byte for
byte. Linking must not buy an exemption from parity, because the surviving copy is
what drifts.

**What this invalidated, checked rather than discovered later.** `orientation.md`
sent readers to `../AGENTS.md` for the risk list three times, including in the
glossary's definition of a risk-gated path. Repointed. While there, a fourth line
in the same paragraph still said `agent_session_driver.py` "routes the result",
which the earlier `is_shim` commit falsified -- now `lifecycle.py`, with the facade
and the launcher named as gated entry points.

Verified: the accept case failed before the change; all four pointer checks pass
after it, and the existing controlled-divergence check still rejects a real
divergence. `make check` green.

Tier: needs-review. `docs_check.py` is gated and these are the governance files.

docs(#261): correct README's ownership claims, archive the vacuous sweep, fix prior-art's two

D4, D6 and D8 -- the doc repairs whose claims could each be checked against a
live source in one step.

**D4, README.** Five corrections, each verified before it was made rather than
after:

- `:49` located the harness at `driver/` and gave it *"outcome classification and
  merge gate"*. `driver/` holds only the compatibility launcher, and the ownership
  is the other way round: `design.md:516` says the driver reads the verdict
  *"rather than re-deriving the gate, so the skill owns the verdict and the driver
  owns only the routing."* The README asserted the inverse of the settled design.
- `:57` said *"Six modes."* `SKILL.md`'s dispatcher lists ten and `phases/` holds
  twelve. Replaced with a pointer to the table rather than a corrected number --
  the count has moved three times and lives in a file that can print it.
- `:157` documented `/agent-session intake` as a slash command. Verified: the skill
  is installed in neither `~/.claude/skills/` nor `~/.codex/skills/`, and
  `orientation.md:106` says so deliberately. Replaced with what you actually do.
- `:168` filed `make check` under "Run the driver over a board" beside `make run`,
  where it reads as one more driver command rather than the whole gate. Given its
  own block. `make loop`'s description no longer hardcodes the queue depth, which
  is now overridable.
- `:190` carried three uncited world-state claims, the last phrased to evade
  `docs_check`'s literal-number pattern. Now points at `make evidence`, which is
  what `CLAUDE.md` instructs twice and what this paragraph was working around.
- `:212` link text said `docs/build-log.md` and the href said
  `docs/archive/build-log.md`.

**D6, the adjacency sweep, archived rather than deleted.** It reports
`adjacent-risk: none` for all 26 rows -- including `threads`, which `findings.md`
documents at length as *the* canonical adjacency instance, and `project-gates`,
which `prior-art.md` independently nominates as another. A sweep asking *"what
could satisfy this row that is not the thing it names?"* that answers "nothing"
against a corpus containing two known instances is a vacuous check in a file:
defect class 6, in the artifact produced for the issue that defines it. It also
reads its conditions out of a `phases/pr.md` that no longer exists, so it could
not be re-run as written.

Kept because **that the sweep ran and produced nothing is itself the finding**, and
deleting it would leave #2 looking closed on evidence that had quietly vanished.
It now carries a banner saying all of that, so it cannot be picked up as live, and
`findings.md`'s ledger row says it too.

**D8, prior-art.** `:180` said a revision-first queue policy was *"a queue policy
our driver does not have and probably needs"* -- `router.py`'s Priority 1 "Unblock"
rung is that policy, and has been. A claim this project falsified itself and never
came back to. `:194` read as a current standing report; dated to when it was
written, so it becomes history rather than a wrong number. `docs-check` caught my
first attempt at that one, which is the escape hatch working as designed.

Tier: auto-ok for D6 and D8 (`docs/`). D4 edits `README.md`, which the allowlist
does not name.

docs(#261): repair findings.md's rotted citations and its self-contradicting counts

D5. The reasoning in this file aged well; its citations and counts did not, and it
misbehaved in exactly the ways it warns about.

**The counts at the front contradicted the file's own rule.** `:21` said "Seven
patterns" over eight numbered sections. `:30` said *"Nine of the eleven below are
fixed; two are open"* over a **twelve**-row table -- and both "open" items were
closed: #2 on the sweep, #79 on the threads row (COMPLETED 2026-08-07). So the
bolded *"The sweep that has never been done"* was false too.

`:118` in this same file says status *"now lives in the table's own column and not
in a sentence above it"*, and `:30` was a sentence above a table carrying status.
Both totals are gone rather than corrected; the sections are numbered and the table
has a status column, so both facts are countable in place.

**The twelfth row was not an instance.** It carried a *filename* in the Instance
column and "Closed by #2" in Status -- the sweep artifact, mis-filed into the
adjacency-instances table, which is what made "eleven" wrong. Removed from the
table and folded into the prose, where it belongs.

**The OPEN GAP header stays, and now says why.** The sweep #2 asked for was run.
Its output answers `adjacent-risk: none` for every row -- including `threads`,
which instance 11 documents at length as the canonical case, and `project-gates`,
which `prior-art.md` nominates as another. A sweep that finds nothing in a corpus
containing two known instances did not look. The issue is closed; the question it
was opened for is not answered, and the entry now states that distinction instead
of claiming the sweep never happened.

**Five dead paths, two of them runnable commands that fail.**
`driver/gate.py` → `src/agent_sessions/driver/gate.py`;
`python3 scripts/commit_lint.py --all` → the module form, verified to run;
`scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py` → `tests/scripts/`.

`driver/test-*.sh` is the interesting one: that is a **file class the conversion
deleted outright**, so the adjacent-assertion rule built on it -- "one grep across
`driver/test-*.sh` and `scripts/test_*.py`" -- had been silently covering half of
what it claimed. Repointed at the live suites; the rule is unchanged, only where it
looks.

`python3 scripts/session_artifact_stats.py` cited a script this audit deleted as
unreachable and broken. The measurement it produced is kept and dated, with a note
that re-running it means writing the script again -- the numbers are the finding,
the script was the instrument.

**Six `phases/pr.md` references, each re-located by hand.** The split into
`open_pr.md` + `grade_gate.md` renumbered the steps, so find-and-replace would have
produced six confident wrong citations. Two describe what the old file said and now
say so; four point at the current phase **by name and rule** rather than by number.
Recorded as a rule above the gotchas, because a wrong step number fails silently --
it still reads like a citation.

**One gotcha's API fact was true and its codebase claim was not.**
`createDiscussionCategory` is still absent from the schema (re-verified against the
live schema), but `ensure_category` no longer calls it -- #211 closed that and it
delegates to `check_category`. The row now separates the two halves and dates each.

**The duplicated "ask what it just invalidated" anecdote defers to CLAUDE.md.** Two
copies existed and the copy here was the stale one, still naming a `driver/gate.py`
path the conversion had superseded while CLAUDE.md's had been updated. The rule
stays here; the worked instance lives in one place. Two copies of a lesson, and the
duplicate rots -- which is the lesson.

Deliberately left alone: `:649`'s "Nine micro-test studies" directly above its
nine-row table. That is a count next to its evidence, which `CLAUDE.md` says is the
correct shape.

Not done here: ~250 lines of this file are now purely historical and belong in
`docs/archive/`. That is a move, not a repair, and it wants its own diff.

Tier: auto-ok. `docs/` is drivable.

Add --repair mode to regenerate truncated alt text

Descriptions written before the reasoning-token fix were cut off
mid-sentence, and the normal scan path cannot reach them: it selects
images whose description is empty, and a truncated fragment is not empty.
Those posts would have stayed broken forever.

--repair inverts the selection. It looks at descriptions that already
exist and regenerates only the ones that were cut off, reusing the
existing fetch/generate/update helpers unchanged.

Detection is deliberately two-stage. A survey of 113 real descriptions
found 38 without closing punctuation, but only 17 were truncated — the
other 21 are hand-written and complete, just terse or unpunctuated.
Regenerating those would discard wording no model can recover from the
image (pet names, "my office", "our living room"). So a free punctuation
prefilter narrows the field, then a text-only LLM judge decides, and the
judge is prompted that missing end punctuation alone does not mean
truncated. It errs toward leaving text alone: a false positive destroys
information, a false negative merely preserves the status quo.

The judge reuses the reasoning_effort passthrough and finish_reason
guard, since a thinking model would otherwise truncate the verdict
itself — the same bug this cleanup exists to undo.

validate_truncation_judge.py scores the judge against all 38 real
descriptions, hand-labelled. At 3 runs per case: 111 judgements, 0 false
positives, 0 false negatives, deterministic. A dry run over 400 posts
agrees — 17 repaired, 21 left intact, 0 errors.

--repair overwrites existing alt text, so it stays out of SCAN_ARGS and
is documented as dry-run-first. Also verified the default missing-alt
path is untouched: old and new selection expressions return identical
results over the same posts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
skills(#261): strip revision history out of the phase files

Les caught this on review, and it is a category error on my part rather than a
style preference.

The phase files are read **by a fresh-context agent, one file at a time, at
runtime**. That reader has no memory of previous revisions, so "this section used
to say X" is pure token cost -- and worse than neutral, because a quoted old value
is a wrong value sitting in context. One of these paragraphs quoted the very label
colour that was wrong.

Everywhere else in this repo the opposite is true. `findings.md` is mostly "here is
what we believed and why it was wrong"; that is what makes it worth reading, and its
audience is a human maintainer. I applied the docs convention to the one place in
the tree where the audience is not a maintainer.

Removed from `SKILL.md`, `execute.md`, `grade_gate.md` (four places), `open_pr.md`,
`rethink.md`, `github-projects.md` and `frozen-checks.md`: what a section used to
say, which issue changed it, and the K-numbers. The provenance is in the commit that
made each change and in #261, both of which persist and are addressed to someone who
wants it.

**Kept: rationale that changes what the agent does.** "Emit `label_create` first,
because otherwise the whole entry fails and the issue is never parked" earns its
tokens -- it is why the step matters. "This used to be absent" does not.

Two rewrites are better rather than merely shorter:

- the `--watch` guidance said a poll loop and a backgrounded shell were *denied*,
  then corrected itself in a parenthetical. It now states the operative fact once:
  they are permitted, and they will still ruin the run, because each poll costs a
  turn. Only `Monitor` is unavailable.
- the ledger instruction in `open_pr.md` explained at length why it had moved there.
  It now just says to append whatever the eventual verdict turns out to be.

Also cleaned one inherited instance in `frozen-checks.md` -- "because `open_pr` no
longer rewrites history" -> "does not rewrite history" -- since it is the same shape
on a line this PR already touches.

Net: 36 fewer added lines across the skill files, and nothing an agent needed.

skills(#261): drop the one pre-existing revision-history note too

`github-projects.md` carried the same shape from before this audit -- a parenthetical
about what an earlier version of the file wrote. Replaced with the thing an agent can
act on: read the board's real option names, because they differ per board.

Two issue citations survive in the skill (`write-manifest.md`'s "issue #191" and
`grade_gate.md`'s "#649 run"). Left alone: they cite a decision and a worked example
rather than narrating a revision, and each is a couple of tokens. Flagged rather than
removed, since where that line falls is a judgment.

Fix alt text truncated mid-sentence by thinking-model reasoning tokens

Thinking models bill reasoning tokens against max_tokens, so with
ALT_TEXT_LLM_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash the invisible reasoning trace starved
the visible answer. The API returned finish_reason="length" and the
description stopped mid-word.

Measured against a LiteLLM proxy: alt text needs only ~8-31 output tokens,
while reasoning consumed 285-894. scan_alt_text.py (max_tokens=300)
truncated on nearly every image, which is the unattended cron path;
app.py (max_tokens=1000) truncated only when reasoning ran long, making
it look intermittent.

Neither call site inspected finish_reason, so truncated fragments were
written to Mastodon as successful updates.

- Pass reasoning_effort through when ALT_TEXT_REASONING_EFFORT is set.
  Omitted when unset, since models without a reasoning mode (the
  gpt-4o-mini default) reject the parameter outright.
- Raise on finish_reason == "length" or empty content instead of
  returning a partial string. This guards the bug class independently of
  model config, so silent truncation cannot reach Mastodon again.
- Document the variable in .env.example, commented out to match the
  non-thinking default model.
- Add diagnose_alt_text.py, which replays the exact request and reports
  the finish_reason and token breakdown the app discards.

Verified against the live proxy: 6/6 complete generations across both
call sites, the guard raises when the variable is removed, and a scanner
dry-run over 25 real posts produced 4 complete descriptions with 0 errors.

Note: "low" reasoning_effort is not sufficient — it still spent 284
reasoning tokens and truncated. Use "disable".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.title: Review: full-repo maintainability and documentation audit (2026-08-19)

labels.name: needs-review
labels.description: A human-judgment criterion or a risk-gated path

issue.body:
## Context

Full-repo maintainability and documentation review, 2026-08-19. Seven parallel reviewers over the
driver core, the scripts package, the test suites, `design.md`/`orientation.md`/`README.md`,
`usage.md`/`findings.md`/`prior-art.md`, `skills/**` plus `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, and build/CI/repo
hygiene. Every claim below was re-verified against the code by hand before landing here; findings
that did not survive verification were dropped.

This issue is the capture record. Items are individually actionable and most want their own PR —
several touch risk-gated paths and cannot be batched with drivable work.

### The one pattern behind most of it

Six of seven reviewers independently found the same shape: **the 2026-08-09 Bash→Python conversion
and the #246/#257/#258 moves relabelled code without moving what pointed at it, and every loose end
fails green.** Six dangling `driver/`-relative paths, none of which turn anything red — an
`is_file()` guard silently skips, `testpaths` exits 0 having run nothing, `docs_check` prints an
honest SKIP that `make check` then ignores, `run_swarm` prints an error where nothing invokes it.

This is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` § *"When you change something, ask what it just invalidated"*
describes, arriving at scale. The structural reason it keeps landing undetected: **`docs_check` only
sees `[text](target)` markdown links, and the skill cites everything in backticks.** Three greps —
over backticked paths, mode names, and label names — would have caught eleven of the sixteen
falsified skill references below.

## Already fixed

On branch `chore/docs-archive-and-build-paths` (not yet PR'd):

- GitHub App private key moved out of the repo root to `~/.config/agent-session/`, `.env` repointed,
  and the `*.private-key.pem` ignore rule committed. It had existed only as an unstaged working-tree
  edit. The key was never committed — verified across every reachable git object.
- 26 pre-2026-08-09 dev-sessions archived to `docs/archive/dev-sessions/` via a new
  `scripts/archive-dev-session.py`. Tracked files under `docs/dev-sessions/` went 326 → 21.
- `pyproject.toml`: `testpaths` repaired (see S3), `pythonpath = ["src"]` added, dead ruff
  per-file-ignores removed, ruff `exclude` extended to `docs/archive`.

---

# Safety

## S1. The merge prohibition has no guard on the REST merge endpoint for the default backend

The complete effective Claude policy at the `Popen` boundary, printed from shipping code:

```
ALLOWED: Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Task,TodoWrite,BashOutput,KillShell,NotebookEdit,Bash(*)
DENIED : Bash(gh pr merge:*), Bash(gh pr merge *), Bash(git push --force:*),
         Bash(gh repo delete:*), Edit/Write/NotebookEdit(<skill_dir>/**)
```

`Bash(*)` is allowed and four patterns are denied. `gh api --method PUT /repos/o/r/pulls/N/merge`
and the `curl` equivalent are **not** among them. `OPENCODE_DENIED_COMMANDS`
(`src/agent_sessions/driver/agent_runner.py:62-63`) *does* deny both, so the non-default backend is
the better-defended one. `git push -f` (short form) is denied on neither — `BASE_DENIED_TOOLS`
spells only `git push --force`.

The only layer that ever covered those vectors is the PreToolUse hook — see S2.

**Fix:** add `gh api *pulls/*/merge*`, `curl *pulls/*/merge*`, and the `-f` short form to
`BASE_DENIED_TOOLS` so Claude's floor matches OpenCode's rather than depending on a hook.
**Tier:** `needs-review` — authorization work on a gated shipping path.

## S2. The PreToolUse merge-block hook has not been installed since the Python conversion

`src/agent_sessions/driver/lifecycle.py:374-375` resolves the hook assets next to itself:

```python
hook_settings_template = Path(__file__).parent / "settings.json"
hook_script = Path(__file__).parent / "merge-block-hook.sh"
```

`src/agent_sessions/driver/` contains only `.py` files; both assets live in repo-root `driver/` and
always have. So `hook_settings_template.is_file()` is False, `state_dir/settings.json` is never
written, and `lifecycle.py:930` passes `--settings <nonexistent path>` to the agent anyway.
`src/agent_sessions/scripts/backend_permission_probe.py:37-38` resolves the same two files
correctly via `PROJECT_ROOT / "driver"`, which is what makes this an oversight rather than a
decision.

Evidence it has been off since 2026-08-09: this repo's `.driver-state/settings.json` is dated Aug 6
— a pre-conversion leftover that happens to point at a real script, which is why nothing has been
observed to break locally. The decafclaw state dir's copy points at
`.worktrees/issue-170/driver/merge-block-hook.sh`, a worktree that no longer exists.

Why no test caught it:
- `tests/driver/test_driver_settings.py:12` asserts the string `--settings` appears in
  `lifecycle.py`'s **source text** — a presence-grep in Python clothing, satisfied by a comment.
  `assertion-lint` cannot see it because it matches only `grep -q`.
- `tests/driver/test_driver_settings.py:26-33` shells out to `jq` and asserts that **jq's assignment
  operator works**. The shipping code renders with `json.loads`/`dumps`. Nothing here calls
  `preflight`.
- `tests/driver/test_merge_hook.py:7` runs the launcher's copy of the script, not the path the
  shipping code resolves.
- `make driver-check` greps only the 8-line compatibility launcher (already tracked by #248).

**Fix:** move the two assets into the package (and ship them as package data), or point
`lifecycle.py` at `PROJECT_ROOT / "driver"` to match the probe. Then **drop the `if ... is_file()`
guard or make the miss loud** — a safety control that silently skips itself when its asset is
missing is the bug behind the bug. Replace the two tests with one that calls `preflight` and asserts
the rendered settings file exists and its `command` points at an executable file.
**Tier:** `needs-review` — gated coordinator, and it is a safety boundary.

## S3. A bare `pytest` reported success having run nothing *(fixed, recorded for the class)*

`pyproject.toml` still read `testpaths = ["driver", "scripts"]` after #257/#258 moved the suites;
both directories now hold only shell assets. `uv run pytest` collected zero tests and **exited 0**.
`make gate-test` passes explicit globs, so CI stayed honest and only the default was a false green.

Fixed on the branch above. Recorded because the class is the point: the relocation commits did not
carry `pyproject.toml`, and no check compares the two. **A guard asserting that a bare `pytest`
collects a non-zero count would close it** — `tests/scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py` already does
exactly that derivation for `make gate-test`, and its globs *were* updated.

## S4. `docs_check`'s assertion-count verification is permanently skipping — second cause

Distinct from #249, which owns the unexpanded-glob half. `src/agent_sessions/scripts/docs_check.py:175`
also passes `scripts/test_*.py`, a path that no longer contains Python. Fixing only the shell
expansion leaves that resolving to nothing, pytest exits 4, `returncode not in (0, 5)` returns
`None`, and the check stays a permanent SKIP. **Both causes have to change**; worth adding to #249
rather than filing separately.

---

# Correctness

## C1. `label_manager` still carries in three commands the bug its own test file documents as fixed

`removable()` (`src/agent_sessions/scripts/label_manager.py:42`) exists because
`gh issue edit --remove-label X` **errors when the repo has no label X at all**, failing the whole
edit including the add. Three commands route through it (`:139`, `:146`, `:169`); three build the
list unconditionally:

- `:115` `cmd_spec`
- `:163` `cmd_attempt`
- `:180` `cmd_merge_ready`

Two of the three survivors are on live paths, both inside `except Exception: pass`:
`src/agent_sessions/driver/parking.py:82` (`attempt --count`) and `parking.py:369`
(`merge-ready`, the `gate-eligible` success path). **On a fresh target repo the attempt label never
lands, the counter never increments, and the loop breaker cannot stop the loop.**

`tests/scripts/test_label_manager.py:1-17` states the diagnosis exactly — *"There were no tests here
at all before this file, which is why three commands carried the same bug"* — then tests only the
three that got the fix. `FakeGh` already reproduces the real `gh` behaviour, so the missing tests are
cheap. **Tier:** `needs-review` (gated `src/**`).

## C2. `make evidence` reads an abandoned state directory

`src/agent_sessions/scripts/evidence.py:34` hardcodes `state_dir = Path(".driver-state")`. The driver
writes to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/agent-session/<repo>/`
(`lifecycle.py:298-306`). Measured: `.driver-state/runs.jsonl` = 38 rows, last written 2026-08-06;
the live ledgers hold 318 real rows. `phase` — the module's primary grouping key — appears in none of
the stale rows, which is why every PHASE cell prints `unknown` today.

This matters more than a normal stale path: `docs_check.check_world_state_claims`
(`docs_check.py:326-329`) fails any bare count in the docs with *"use `make evidence` instead"*. The
doc-rot detector's prescribed remedy is reporting dead data, and `design.md:382` and
`orientation.md:350` both cite it as *"the only authoritative source for what has actually run."*

**Ordering constraint — do C3 first.** The live ledger currently contains ~1700 fabricated
`owner/repo` rows from the test suite, so repointing `evidence.py` before fixing test isolation
launders fixture data into the evidence report. **Tier:** `needs-review`.

## C3. The test suite writes into the operator's real `$HOME`; there is no `conftest.py`

There is **no `conftest.py` anywhere in the repo**, so nothing pins `XDG_STATE_HOME`. The fixture
repo `owner/repo` (`tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:64`) therefore resolves to a real path:

```
~/.local/state/agent-session/owner-repo/    11M, 872 run dirs, runs.jsonl ≈ 1700 rows
                                            plus inbox.md, parked.jsonl, workspaces/
```

Some suites do redirect individually (`tests/scripts/test_run_progress.py:177`,
`tests/driver/test_driver.py:465`); `test_full_loop.py` does not. Consequences: unbounded growth in
`$HOME`, non-hermetic tests that can read state left by earlier runs, and the C2 ordering problem.
The untracked `.local/` directory in the repo root is spill from the same non-hermeticity — benign
today (`gh` device-id), but the same misdirected `HOME` would equally write `gh`'s `hosts.yml`, which
holds OAuth tokens, into an unignored directory.

**Fix:** an autouse session fixture in a new `tests/conftest.py` pinning `XDG_STATE_HOME` to
`tmp_path`; delete `~/.local/state/agent-session/owner-repo/`; add `.local/` and `runs/` to
`.gitignore`. **Tier:** `auto-ok` — `tests/**` is drivable and the check is mechanical.

## C4. The full-loop suite's lock-isolation is inert, and the leak fires real `git push` at exit

`tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:735-737`:

```python
# The driver releases its lock from an atexit hook keyed on this global.
# monkeypatch restores it to None, so no pass can leave a live lock behind.
monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE", None)
```

The comment is wrong. `agent_session_driver.py:48` does `from ...locks import CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE`,
binding a **copy** of a `str | None`; `locks.release_lock`/`acquire_lock` read and write
`locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` via `global`. Nothing in `src/` reads the re-exported name. Demonstrated:
patching the barrel leaves `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` untouched.

Observable on every suite run — these are the `atexit` hook firing at worker shutdown, *after*
monkeypatch has restored the real `subprocess.run`:

```
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #102...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #101...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #109...
```

Harmless today only because the `tmp_path` repos have no `origin`. A test that ever pointed
`--repo-path` at a real checkout would push a ref deletion to a real remote from a test process.

**Fix:** patch `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` (the owning module) or add `locks.reset()`; add an autouse
teardown asserting it is `None`; drop `CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` from the barrel's re-exports so nobody
re-derives the wrong seam. **Tier:** `auto-ok` for the test half.

## C5. `gate.extract_gate` and `gate.budget_reclass` are tested but unreachable from a run

- `lifecycle.py:485` and `:1072` both call `gate.classify(pr_body, ...)`. `extract_gate` is called
  only from `gate.py`'s own CLI and from `tests/driver/test_gate.py` (~15 sites, always as
  `classify(extract_gate(body))`). So the tests exercise `extract_gate → classify` while production
  runs `classify(whole_body)`. `has_gate = bool(body.strip())` is then true for any non-empty PR
  body, and `gate_fields()` (`gate.py:186`) harvests every `key: value` line anywhere in it. It
  mostly still lands on `no-gate` via `validate_gate_block`, which is why it hasn't bitten — but the
  tested path and the run path differ **at the oracle**.
- `lifecycle.py:1084-1086` reimplements the budget rule inline while `gate.budget_reclass()`
  (`gate.py:592-604`) — with `_NO_VERDICT_OUTCOMES` and a 9-line docstring recording why the
  threshold is 95% — is referenced only from `gate.py`'s CLI and `test_gate.py:237`. The tested,
  documented implementation is unreachable; the live one is an untested literal.

**Fix:** call `gate.classify(gate.extract_gate(pr_body), ...)` at both sites (with a fixture proving
before/after on a real PR body), and replace the inline threshold with `gate.budget_reclass(...)`.
Note the second **moves** a threshold out of the coordinator into gated `gate.py` — a tightening,
not a widening, but say so in the PR. **Tier:** `needs-review` — the oracle.

## C6. Two skill phase files write label names the harness has never heard of

`skills/agent-session/phases/triage.md`:
- `:59`, `:95` — records `agent-session:needs-details`. `rg 'needs-details' src/` returns nothing.
- `:97` — records `agent-session:interactive`. The real name is
  `agent-session:needs-human-interactive` (`label_manager.py:16`, `parking.py:14`).

`src/agent_sessions/driver/writes.py:295` executes a `label` entry as one
`gh issue edit --add-label A --add-label B` with no ensure-exists, and `gh` errors when the repo has
no such label — so **the whole edit fails and the issue is never parked**, and
`write-manifest.md:43` then stops the rest of the manifest. `:97` compounds it with *"instead"*,
which leaves the issue carrying **no** park label, so the router keeps re-selecting it.
`intake.md:81` gets this right by emitting a `label_create` first; `triage.md` never does.

**Tier:** `needs-review` — `skills/**` is hard-gated.

## C7. Three scripts carry a repo-root derivation that is wrong post-src-layout

| site | expression | resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| `guard_lint.py:19` | `.parent.parent` | `src/agent_sessions` (unused, harmless) |
| `session_artifact_stats.py:16` | `.parent.parent` | `src/agent_sessions` (load-bearing) |
| `run_swarm.py:21` | `SCRIPTS_DIR.parent` | `src/agent_sessions` (load-bearing) |

Correct is `parents[3]`, as in `docs_check.py:44`, `assertion_lint.py:66`, `state_diagram.py:21`,
`backend_permission_probe.py:15`. Verified live:

```
$ uv run python -m agent_sessions.scripts.session_artifact_stats
Error: .../src/agent_sessions/docs/dev-sessions does not exist        exit=1
```

`run_swarm.py:59` additionally looks for `ROOT_DIR / "driver" / "agent_runner.py"`, deleted by the
conversion, and aborts every time. Its only reference is
`skills/agent-session/phases/execute.md:49`, which invokes the equally-gone
`python3 scripts/run_swarm.py`. **Both `run_swarm.py` and `session_artifact_stats.py` are
unreachable through any current entry point and broken if reached** — deleting them (plus the
`execute.md` reference, a gated skill edit) is a smaller change than fixing them. If `run_swarm`
goes, `validate_tdd.py` goes with it, and C8 becomes moot.

## C8. `validate_tdd` grades a stream it never read as compliant

`src/agent_sessions/scripts/validate_tdd.py:13-14` returns `True` for a missing stream, and
`run_swarm.py:114` double-guards the same null in the same unsafe direction
(`validate_stream(raw) if raw.exists() else True`). A subagent that crashed before writing anything
passes the TDD discipline check twice over. `tests/scripts/test_validate_tdd.py:98-100` enshrines
the fail-open, and `tests/scripts/test_run_swarm.py:25-45` never writes a stream, so
`assert data["passed"] is True` would hold with `validate_stream` deleted from the module.
Also `:65` treats any Bash output containing `FAIL` as a failing check, so `--tb=no` output
mentioning `FAILURES` satisfies the red phase.

Distinct from #249: there the check says it skipped; here it returns a **positive** and nothing
records that no evidence was examined. **Policy call for a human** — tri-state, or delete with C7.

## C9. `label_manager.get_current_labels` swallows every failure, so the transition guard permits

`src/agent_sessions/scripts/label_manager.py:69-76` returns `[]` on any exception. `main():229` feeds
that to `validate_transition():83`, which computes `is_parked = PARK_LABEL in current_labels`. A
transient rate-limit, auth or network failure therefore yields `is_parked = False` and a **parked
issue gets re-specced or re-attempted**. `board_audit.run_gh` (`:57-59`) raises on any nonzero exit;
the package already knows the right shape. Same file, `ensure_label_exists:36-39` swallows
`RuntimeError` unconditionally, making a 403 indistinguishable from "already exists".

## C10. `make guard-lint` scans at most 30 issues and reports a clean bill

`Makefile:145` pipes `gh issue list --json body` with no `--limit`; `gh`'s default is 30. On a repo
with more open issues the detector examines the newest 30 and prints *"no pinned test count guards
found"* — a null rendering as a positive, in a repo whose thesis is that this must not happen.
`board_audit` already solved it with `--limit 500` plus `bounded_records` raising at the limit.
`guard_lint` has no idea how many records it was handed. Not in `make check`, hence the rank.

## C11. `test_docs_check.py` clones the detector instead of calling it, and the clone has drifted

`tests/scripts/test_docs_check.py:62-100` reimplements `docs_check.check_world_state_claims` as a
local `check_line()` and asserts against the copy; `docs_check` is never called. Proven drift:

```
'Runs against many repositories'   test-copy: ['many repositories']  shipped-regex: False
```

The shipped pattern is `\b(one|two|…|ten|\d+) repositories\b`; the copy is `\b([a-z]+) repositories\b`.
The copy also carries an exemption the shipped code lacks and omits two the shipped code has, and
the shipped table's 2-tuples make the `cond = item[2:]` predicate path at `docs_check.py:369-374`
permanently dead — the mechanism exists only in the test. **`check_world_state_claims` — the newest
docs-check rule — has zero coverage through shipping code.** Delete `check_line` and the suite stays
green. This is defect class 1 instance 9 verbatim, inside the doc-rot detector's own suite, and it is
the residual risk `CLAUDE.md` names about leaving `tests/**` drivable.

`mypy src tests` (as opposed to the `mypy src` that `make typecheck` runs) flags this file at
`:84-86` with `"str" not callable`, which is the same defect surfacing as a type error.

---

# Structural

## T1. `agent_session_driver.py` is a re-export barrel that the package calls back through

143 lines that **define nothing** — an import list plus a 58-entry `__all__` and
`if __name__ == "__main__"`. Its `__all__` re-exports the standard library (`"datetime"`,
`"timezone"`) to serve **one line**: `tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:734` freezing time via
`monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "datetime", FrozenDatetime)`. To make that reachable,
`lifecycle.log()` and `locks.log()` each do a function-local import of the barrel purely to fetch
`agent_session_driver.datetime`.

`lifecycle.py` calls back through the barrel **44 times**, including `agent_session_driver.whoami` at
`:270` for a function defined at `lifecycle.py:146` — lifecycle calling itself via a module that
imports it. The cycle survives only because four modules defer their imports into function bodies
(14 sites across `lifecycle`, `board`, `parking`, `locks`). `board.say()` reaches the barrel, which
re-exports `lifecycle.say`, to write one line to stdout — while `lifecycle`, `parking` and
`pr_checks` define a **second, divergent** `say` that writes to stdout directly, so output behaviour
depends on which module you are in. Five spellings of one output helper set (four `say`, two `log`,
two `die`).

Read: **#246's decomposition is half-landed.** It extracted `RunContext` and named the lifecycle
operations, but kept the old god-module as a compatibility barrel so existing tests would not need
rewriting — and the modules now reach back through it. The seams were named without being cut. C4 is
the first concrete cost.

`agent_session_driver.py:14` also carries `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))`, a
pre-package fossil that puts the package directory on `sys.path`, making `board`, `locks`, `gate`,
`router`, `credentials` importable as top-level names. Nothing needs it.

**Fix, smallest first:** a tiny `driver/output.py` (`say`/`log`/`die`, no driver imports) that all
six modules import — this alone breaks three of `board.py`'s four barrel dependencies. Then move the
time seam to the owning module and delete the barrel's stdlib re-exports. Do **not** attempt full
de-shimming as unattended work. Distinct from #247, which is about the *GitHub I/O* surface; this is
the intra-package call graph. **Tier:** `needs-review` — gated file.

## T2. The lifecycle operations were named but not decomposed

`invoke_agent` 286 lines, `preflight` 230, `classify_and_record` 186, `select_queue` 162; and
`router.select` is a single 222-line function. The four-function shape from #246 is sound and I am
not proposing more than two extractions, each with an obvious seam:

- `lifecycle.py:700-813` — three independent GitHub reads appending to one `extra_context` string →
  `gather_extra_context(ctx, issue_num, phase, open_prs) -> str`
- `lifecycle.py:849-899` — the whole deterministic `request_review` branch → `run_request_review(...)`

That is ~170 of `invoke_agent`'s 286 lines, both testable in isolation. `preflight`'s inflight/orphan
warning (`:343-369`) and hook-settings block (`:371-385`) come out cleanly too.

## T3. Duplication worth collapsing

- **`gate.py:252-303` vs `:306-403`** — `verify_gate_rows` and `infer_provenance` encode the same
  seven row predicates twice, line for line, differing only in what they emit. Change a rule in one
  and the verdict disagrees with its own provenance record, **on the oracle**. Fix: one
  `_row_state(field, value)` per row consumed by both. `test_gate.py` already covers both.
- **`router.py:63-101` vs `lifecycle.py:521-555`** — `board_nums`, the priority-label filter,
  `is_specced`, and `candidates_json`/`markerless_json` are each computed twice. `router.py:85-90`
  reimplements `parking.is_specced` with inlined literals while `parking.py:16-17` defines
  `SPEC_LABEL`/`MARKER`, and `router.py:16-17` shadows `parking.py`'s `PARK_LABEL`/`MERGE_READY_LABEL`.
  **A label rename now needs four edits and fails open** (issues silently stop being selected).
  Label constants are triplicated across `label_manager.py:12-22`, `parking.py:13-16`,
  `router.py:16-17`.
- **`parking.py:60-68, 73-81, 88-99, 103-111, 115-123, 369-377`** — six copies of the same seven-line
  `label_manager.py` subprocess block, four of which discard the failure entirely. `label_manager`
  exposes an importable `main(argv) -> int`; a typed call returning 1 is hard to ignore, a swallowed
  `CalledProcessError` is the default. This is *why* C1 and C9 are invisible.
- **`parking.py:126-268`** — `has_new_human_comment` implements the same comment/reaction scan twice
  (GraphQL and REST branches) with four copies of the same timestamp-normalisation triple-replace, in
  one 143-line function. Extraction takes it to ~60 lines.
- **`lifecycle.py:462-490` vs `:1044-1080`** — `run_classify_only` duplicates the tail of
  `classify_and_record`; the recovery path and the normal path can drift, and per C5 they already
  differ from the tested path together.
- **Three incompatible `gh` wrappers** — `board_audit.run_gh:49` (raises, decodes JSON),
  `label_manager.run_gh:25` (raises `RuntimeError`, returns text), `doctor._gh:88` (injects tokens,
  returns raw `CompletedProcess`, never checks `returncode` — callers use
  `getattr(res, "returncode", 1)` at eleven sites). They differ on the three things that matter:
  token injection, error propagation, truncation. Lower priority than the correctness items: the
  divergences are mostly deliberate.
- **Four JSONL readers, four tolerance policies** — `run_progress.read_records:87-114` is the good
  one and documents why; `evidence.py:42-50`, `validate_tdd.py:17-25`, and
  `backend_permission_probe.observed_denials:69-74` each re-derive it worse. The last calls `.get`
  on records `json.loads` may have returned as `str` or `int`.

## T4. Dead code left by the conversion and the #246 split

- `SelectionResult.board_items` / `.open_issues` (`lifecycle.py:74-75`) — populated at `:661-662`,
  read by nobody.
- `InvocationResult.writes_file` / `.run_repo_path` (`lifecycle.py:88,96`) — set at `:955,962`, never
  read.
- `parking.clear_attempt_labels` (`:59`) — referenced only by the barrel's import and `__all__`.
- `router.py:106` declares `p4_escalate` and **never appends to it**; `:210` concatenates an
  always-empty list. `design.md:340` documents P4 as a real priority.
- `agent_runner.py:21-28` — an `ImportError` fallback that re-imports the module from the same
  package path that just failed, for a `python agent_runner.py` invocation nothing performs.
- `agent_runner.py:565` — `_main(argv)` never touches `argv`; the body reads `sys.argv`.
- `discussion_manager.py:76` — unused `emoji` parameter, and a "Deprecated alias" docstring on what
  is now the supported entry point (via `scripts/bootstrap-repo.sh:56`).
- `Makefile:41` — `.PHONY: ... driver-test-sh` names a target with **no rule anywhere**. It exists in
  the target database only because `.PHONY` names it, and `make driver-test-sh` exits 0 having done
  nothing. Bash-era leftover.

## T5. `perform_writes` mutates the shape it returns

`pr_checks.py:193-195` bolts `messages`, `entries`, `applied` onto the dict `writes.execute` returned
(`writes.py:405`, keys `ok`/`errors`/`results`). Both are annotated bare `dict`, so mypy sees
`dict[Any, Any]` and `inv.writes_result["applied"]` (`lifecycle.py:988`) is unchecked. A `TypedDict`
per shape would catch a key typo. Minor: `RunContext.workspaces_dir: str` (`lifecycle.py:66`) is the
one path-shaped field typed `str` among nine `Path` neighbours, so both consumers repeat
`Path(ctx.workspaces_dir).resolve() if ... else None`.

## T6. `reconciler.py`'s webhook half has no host

`run_webhook_reconciler`, `parse_webhook_event`, `handle_event`, `handle_issue_comment`, and
`PollingAdapter.synthesize_comment_event` are referenced only within `reconciler.py` and its tests;
`.github/workflows/` has only `check.yml`. Production uses only `synthesize_pr_event` +
`handle_pr_reconcile`. **Keep it** — pure, cheap, tested, and named in `design.md` as the reactive
path — but `run_webhook_reconciler:278-279` should not claim `"acquired_git_lock": True` when it
acquires nothing.

---

# Tests

## X1. `assertion-lint` covers 15 of 33 test files, and would not have caught either real instance

`assertion_lint.py:81` sets `SCOPE = "tests/driver/test_*.py"`; all 18 files under `tests/scripts/`
are unlinted. Both S2's presence-grep and C11's cloned detector use Python `in` against
`read_text()`, not `grep -q`, so the linter would miss them even in scope. **Two things for a human:**
widening `SCOPE` to `tests/{driver,scripts}/test_*.py`, and adding a rule for
`assert <literal> in <source_text>` where the right-hand side came from reading a repo file. The
second is the pattern that actually bit. The docstring's own warning about false positives training
the operator to wave the check through is the reason this is a judgment call.

## X2. Two weak GitHub fakes sit beside the strong one

`tests/driver/test_workspace_driver_integration.py:52-65,122-126,185-192` and
`tests/driver/test_driver.py:445-457,487-508,542-552` monkeypatch `subprocess.run` with a catch-all
`MockResult` (`stdout = "{}"`, `returncode = 0`) that answers **every** unmodelled `gh` call with
success. `test_full_loop.py`'s docstring (lines 20-31) names this exact anti-pattern as the reason
`FakeGitHub.unhandled` and `field_gaps` exist. `test_workspace_driver_integration.py` would pass if
the driver started issuing a completely different set of GitHub calls. Plus `test_driver.py:433-601`
repeats ~25 lines of setup verbatim three times.

## X3. No `conftest.py`; the `sys.path` bootstrap is copy-pasted 24 times

`sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "src"))` appears in 24 files while nine
others import `agent_sessions` with no bootstrap, so the split is arbitrary. `pythonpath = ["src"]`
(landed on the branch above) makes all 24 deletable. `dummy_git_repo` is byte-identical in
`tests/driver/test_workspace.py:27-37` and `test_workspace_driver_integration.py:10-20`. Moving
`FakeGitHub`/`StubAgent`/`LoopHarness` into `tests/driver/conftest.py` is the prerequisite for fixing
X2.

## X4. Coverage gaps that matter

- **`--classify-only` has zero coverage.** The flag appears only in `lifecycle.py`. This is the
  branch an operator reaches for *after* a run dies mid-flight — `lifecycle.py:360-369` prints it as
  the recovery instruction three times.
- **`locks.py:120-152`'s stale-lock steal and TTL are untested.** No test references
  `force-with-lease`, `ttl`, or the steal path. Untested: `lock_age >= ttl_seconds` → force-with-lease
  push; the 600s/7200s split by phase (`locks.py:71`); a lease that *loses* the race; `release_lock`
  itself. This is the distributed mutual-exclusion primitive — get the TTL wrong and two drivers run
  the same issue, spending budget twice. `FakeGitHub.held_locks` already takes a timestamp, so the
  steal case is a one-line fixture change.

## X5. Slow, fragile, and CWD-dependent tests

- **One test is 85% of the wall clock.** `test_gate_test_wiring.py::test_new_test_file_runs_under_gate_test_with_no_makefile_edit`
  takes 30.3s of a 35.6s run because it invokes `make gate-test` twice for real — so `make check`
  runs the whole suite three times over. **Do not weaken it**; it is the only thing standing between
  you and a test file that silently never runs. Worth knowing the floor is ~3×, and worth an `-x` on
  the with-probe arm, which only needs to observe one failure.
- `xdist_group` at `test_gate_test_wiring.py:44` is **inert** — it is honoured only under
  `--dist loadgroup`, and `make gate-test` runs `-n auto` with no `--dist`. C1 and C2 can land on
  different workers and run concurrently while C2 writes a probe file into the tree C1 is collecting.
  Masked today by the process-unique probe name.
- No git-config isolation in any `git init` fixture: no `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, no
  `commit.gpgsign=false`. A developer or CI image with global `commit.gpgsign` or `core.hooksPath`
  breaks eight tests in a way that reads as a code failure.
- CWD-relative paths in `test_driver_settings.py:8,10,15,23,24`, `test_merge_hook.py:7,13,19,25,30`,
  `test_board_audit.py:443,563`, `test_gate.py:222,551`, while every other suite derives
  `parents[2]`. `test_driver_settings.py:9-10` silently falls back to a *different* file if
  `lifecycle.py` is missing, so a rename makes it grade the wrong artifact rather than fail. It also
  requires `jq` on `$PATH`.
- `test_evidence.py:27,40,46` replaces `builtins.open` and `Path.is_file` process-wide;
  `test_discussion_manager.py:16-17` builds expected titles from the real wall clock, so crossing UTC
  midnight between two calls fails the test.
- Vacuous: `test_writes.py:93` (`assert spec is not None` over `KINDS.items()`),
  `test_driver.py:527` (`isinstance(..., list)` immediately before a length assertion),
  `test_docs_check.py:36,52` (defensive `getattr` then `assert ... is not None`).

**On `test_full_loop.py`: I would argue against splitting it.** 1594 lines, but one harness, one
fake, one stub agent, and five explicitly labelled case groups whose seam is *the driver pass*, not a
module. Its assertions are whole-object equality on `runs.jsonl` rows and whole-list equality on
`label_ops`, and `LoopHarness.run` asserts `gh.unhandled == []` and `gh.field_gaps == []` on every
pass. Extract the harness to `conftest.py`; leave the bodies together.

---

comment.body:
## X1 — repurposed rather than widened or deleted

`assertion-lint` now carries two rules. The change is on
`refactor/261-assertion-lint-repurpose`, at the tip of the stack.

### Rule 1 had lost its subject

It detects `grep -q 'literal' "$FILE"`. The Bash fixture suites it was written for were
deleted by the 2026-08-09 conversion, and there is **not one occurrence anywhere under
`tests/`** outside the detector's own fixtures — nor can there be, since Python tests
don't shell out to grep. `no presence-grep assertions in 18 file(s)` was a green that
could not have been anything else. Defect class 6, inside a detector.

Kept as a cheap regression guard if a shell fixture ever returns.

### Rule 2 is the same class in the language the suites are written in

```
assert "some literal" in SOME_CHECKED_IN_FILE.read_text()
```

**Two live instances, both written during this audit, by the session auditing for
them, hours apart:**

| Where | Satisfied by |
|---|---|
| `test_gate_test_wiring.py` — `"--dist loadgroup" in joined` | a `# needs --dist loadgroup` comment in the recipe |
| `test_bootstrap_repo.py` — module path `in src` | the comment three lines above it, which says exactly that |

Both now grade structure: the wiring check parses `--dist` and its value; the bootstrap
check reads the invocation line and requires `-m` with the dotted module and no `.py`
path.

### Why two stages, and what each one buys

X1 proposed tracing each assertion's right-hand side back to a `read_text()`. Measured:
**ten flagged, one real** — assertions on *generated* output (a prompt a run wrote, a
rendered diagram) are indistinguishable at that level.

Filtering first on whether the **module** reads a checked-in artifact drops all of those
in one move. On the live tree: **four flagged, two real**, and the other two were
converted anyway because parsing is stronger — `"--issue 704" in text` is satisfied by
`--issue 7040`, and reading the flag's value is not.

### This also answers the widening question

Rule 2 **needs no narrowed glob**. `commit_lint.py` records that `assertion_lint` "had to
solve the same self-matching problem by narrowing its glob" — true of a *textual* rule
whose own fixtures contain the idiom. An AST rule sees a fixture as a string constant and
a real assertion as an `Assert` node. So rule 2 scans every test file in the repo,
including its own, and rule 1 stays narrow. Widening *rule 1* remains declined on the
measurement: six hits, all six in this detector's fixtures, zero real findings.

### Two narrowings the rule earned by being wrong

Worth recording, because both are cases of the instrument being wrong in a way that would
have got it switched off:

- It flagged `assert "-m" in tokens` — the parsed-structure form it *recommends as the
  remedy*. An instrument that punishes its own fix doesn't survive. Membership against a
  sequence of tokens is now excluded.
- It flagged `assert "--dry-run" in _expanded(dry)`, where `_expanded(...) -> list[str]`.
  Already a token test, and the annotation was right there. Not reading it made the rule
  invite a "fix" that broke the assertion — which I made, then backed out. Local helpers
  annotated as returning a sequence are now read.

Verified: the detector fails on both real instances when they're restored, and on neither
legitimate token assertion. `make check` green from a cold `.venv`, 688 tests.

issue.body:
## Context

Full-repo maintainability and documentation review, 2026-08-19. Seven parallel reviewers over the

### The one pattern behind most of it
