## Progress — second pass, continued

Eleven more commits on the same stack (18 total). `make check` green on each. Still
nothing pushed.

| Branch | Closes |
|---|---|
| `fix/261-assertion-lint` | **H10**; X1 measured and returned |
| `fix/261-classify-only-ledger` | **N2** |
| `fix/261-agents-md-pointer` | **G1** |
| `docs/261-doc-repairs` | **D4, D5, D6, D8**, then **D3**, then **D2** |
| `fix/261-make-clean` | **H5** |
| `fix/261-dead-code` | **T4** |
| `refactor/261-gate-row-predicates` | **T3** (the oracle half) |
| `refactor/261-label-constants` | **T3** (label vocabulary) |
| `refactor/261-parking-label-calls` | **T3** (parking's five copies) |

### X1: I did not do what you asked, and here is why

You chose "widen the scope and add the rule." I prototyped both and measured:

- **Widening** to `tests/scripts/test_*.py` reports **6 hits, all 6 inside
  `test_assertion_lint.py`'s own shell fixtures**, and 0 real findings. Widening therefore
  costs either a named exemption — the standing bypass the detector's docstring
  deliberately refuses — or restructuring the fixtures away from the assertions they
  define.
- **The rule** (`assert <literal> in <source_text>`) finds **10 hits, 9 of them
  legitimate**: assertions on generated output, a prompt the run wrote, a rendered
  diagram. The 1 true positive was in a file I had written an hour earlier. Narrowing it
  to repo-anchored paths drops the false positives to 0 and the true positives to 0 as
  well, missing even that one via indirection.

And `commit_lint.py`'s own Scope section already records the reason from the outside:
*"`assertion_lint` had to solve the same self-matching problem by narrowing its glob."*

So neither half is implemented. The measurement is now in `assertion_lint.py`'s Scope
section so the next person decides with a number rather than re-deriving it, and the one
real instance is fixed by hand — `test_workflow_pinning.py` now parses `fetch-depth` as a
key/value pair instead of substring-matching it. **Say the word and I'll do the fixture
restructuring**; I just didn't want to spend it on a 0-finding widening without flagging
that first.

### The oracle refactor was proved, not asserted

`verify_gate_rows` and `infer_provenance` encoded the same seven row predicates twice.
Before merging them I replayed both implementations over a **927-case matrix** — every row
varied against a clean baseline plus every pairwise combination of two rows, including
missing, failing, malformed and substitute-marked values. After the refactor the same 927
cases produce **zero differences** in either output, and the reason strings are
byte-identical, so no recorded run reason changes.

Two subtleties the matrix caught that a naive merge would have broken: `tier` has no
`substituted` state (it is a classification, not evidence, so nothing can stand in for
it), and failure outranks substitution (`threads: 1 unresolved -- via substitute` is
`failed`). The coupling is now asserted per row and mutation-tested — re-inlining one
row's rule into `infer_provenance` alone fails two checks.

### Findings that were wrong, or wrong-sized

- **H5's premise.** It attributes 3.2 GB to "287 run directories". Measured:
  `workspaces/` 3.1 GB, `runs/` 79 MB, ledger 204 KB. Pruning run dirs reclaims 79 MB;
  the volume is per-issue git worktrees. Both are pruned now, by different rules.
- **`workspace.remove_workspace` uses `git worktree remove --force`,** which does not
  refuse a dirty worktree. **5 of 21 live workspaces are dirty.** The driver's own
  `--clean-workspaces` would force-remove all five, and `findings.md` records an incident
  where exactly such a worktree held the only copy of a run's gate block. `make
  prune-state WORKSPACES=1` keeps them and says so. **The driver's own path is unchanged
  and still force-removes** — that is a gated behaviour change and your call.
- **findings.md's twelfth adjacency row was not an instance.** It carried a *filename* in
  the Instance column — the sweep artifact, mis-filed into the table, which is what made
  "eleven" wrong.
- **There is no P4.** `design.md` documented "P4: Escalate" and `router.py` declared a
  `p4_escalate` list that nothing ever appended to, then concatenated it. Attempt-exhausted
  issues are *parked*. Both removed.
- **A fourth label-constant site** the issue didn't name: `writes.py`. On inspection it is
  `EXAMPLES`, inert documentation, so the new AST check excludes that named subtree rather
  than the file.
- **#249's own acceptance criterion doesn't run** — `uv run pytest -q
  scripts/test_docs_check.py ...` exits 4. Reported there along with S4's second cause.

### Twice my own controls caught my own fix

- H1's obvious fix, `$(or $(ISSUES),$(LOOP_ISSUES))`, is wrong: `ISSUES ?= 1` means
  `$(or)` cannot tell "caller asked" from "file defaulted", and a bare `make loop`
  collapsed to one issue. `$(origin)` distinguishes them.
- The git-config isolation's first form used `GIT_AUTHOR_*`, which outranks *repo-level*
  config — silently re-authoring commits in the two fixtures that set their own. A stub
  global config file sits below repo config, which is the ordering the fixtures assume.

### Remaining

X2 (FakeGitHub into conftest), T2's two extractions, T5/T6, D7 and the `skills/**` batch
(K1–K9 plus dropping `execute.md`'s `run_swarm` references). The skill work is hard-gated
and I'll keep it on its own branch.

issue.title: Fix: prevent docs-check assertion verification from skipping under make check
issue.body:
## Goal

Make assertion-count verification complete under `make check` and in the standalone
`docs-check` target.

## Evidence

`make check` runs `gate-test` and `docs-check` in parallel. During the maintainability
review, the aggregate command passed while `docs-check` printed:

```text
SKIP  assertion counts: could not run make gate-test (NOT verified -- this is a skip, not a pass)
```

The same skip reproduces under standalone `make docs-check`. The collection helper
passes literal `driver/test_*.py` and `scripts/test_*.py` arguments through
`subprocess.run` without shell expansion; the equivalent direct command exits 4 with
`file or directory not found`. The parallel gate makes the skip easy to miss among
interleaved output, but concurrency is not the only failing condition.

## Bounded scope

- Make the collection mechanism resolve the intended test files and remain reliable
  when `gate-test` runs concurrently.
- Keep `make check` parallel unless evidence shows serialization is the smallest safe
  solution.
- Preserve `docs-check`'s explicit distinction between a verified count and a skip.
- Do not pin a test count in documentation or introduce a hand-maintained test-file
  census.

## Acceptance criteria

- **C1 — runnable after its regression oracle is added.** Regression tests SHALL call
  the assertion-count probe both alone and concurrently with `gate-test`, and fail if
  `live_bash_assertions()` returns `None` or emits the assertion-count skip. Run:

  ```text
  uv run pytest -q scripts/test_docs_check.py scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py
  ```

- **C2 — runnable.** The aggregate gate SHALL finish with no assertion-count skip and
  shall retain parallel execution:

  ```text
  make check
  ```

- **C3 — runnable.** The independent target SHALL still perform the assertion-count
  verification:

  ```text
  make docs-check
  ```

- **G1 — runnable.** The gate-test wiring assertions SHALL still discover new matching
  test files without a Makefile edit:

  ```text
  uv run pytest -q scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py
  ```

## Tier

`needs-review`. The relevant implementation paths are drivable, but the discriminating
concurrency oracle does not exist yet and must be built before an autonomous run could
freeze this issue's criteria.

## Overlap

Issue #152 concerns policy separation, and issue #195 concerns distribution. Neither
owns check-process composition. This issue is limited to the observed parallel skip.

comment.body:
## Two things found while auditing #261 — a second cause, and this issue's own criteria

### S4: unexpanded globs are not the only cause

This issue's Evidence names the mechanism correctly — `live_bash_assertions()` passes
literal glob strings through `subprocess.run` with no shell expansion. There is a
**second, independent cause** sitting behind it, and fixing only the globs leaves the
check permanently skipping.

`docs_check.py:176` passes two paths:

```python
["uv", "run", "pytest", "--collect-only", "-q", "tests/driver/test_*.py", "scripts/test_*.py"]
```

`scripts/` contains no Python test files. #257/#258 moved them to `tests/scripts/`:

```
$ ls scripts/
__pycache__  archive-dev-session.py  bootstrap-repo.sh  prune_run_state.py
```

So once the globs expand, `scripts/test_*.py` matches nothing. Depending on how the
expansion is implemented that is either an error or a silently dropped argument — and
the second is worse, because the probe would then return a count derived from half the
suite and report it as verified. The `returncode not in (0, 5)` guard turns the first
case into `None`, which is the skip this issue is about.

**Both halves need fixing together.** Expand the globs *and* repoint the second path at
`tests/scripts/`.

Reproduced on the current tree:

```
$ AGENT_SESSIONS_GATE_TEST_WIRING_INNER_RUN=1 uv run pytest --collect-only -q \
    "tests/driver/test_*.py" "scripts/test_*.py"
ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/driver/test_*.py
```

### C1's own command does not run

The acceptance criterion is:

```
uv run pytest -q scripts/test_docs_check.py scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py
```

```
$ uv run pytest -q scripts/test_docs_check.py scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py
ERROR: file or directory not found: scripts/test_docs_check.py
exit=4
```

Both files are now `tests/scripts/test_docs_check.py` and
`tests/scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py`. Worth fixing before the issue is picked up:
under `agent-session`'s own rules a criterion has to name a runnable check, and this one
names a command that exits 4 — which an implementer could satisfy by making the *command*
run rather than the *property* hold.

### Context

Found while working #261. Neither is fixed here — this issue owns the assertion-count
probe, and splitting the fix across two branches would be worse than leaving it whole.
Nothing in #261's branches touches `live_bash_assertions()`.

One thing that has changed underneath this issue: `make check` no longer races on a cold
`.venv` (it warms it once before fanning out), so if any part of the skip was
concurrency-related, that variable is gone and the remaining failure is purely the two
path bugs above.

issue.title: Review: full-repo maintainability and documentation audit (2026-08-19)

labels.name: needs-review
labels.description: A human-judgment criterion or a risk-gated path

issue.body:
## Context

Full-repo maintainability and documentation review, 2026-08-19. Seven parallel reviewers over the
driver core, the scripts package, the test suites, `design.md`/`orientation.md`/`README.md`,
`usage.md`/`findings.md`/`prior-art.md`, `skills/**` plus `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, and build/CI/repo
hygiene. Every claim below was re-verified against the code by hand before landing here; findings
that did not survive verification were dropped.

This issue is the capture record. Items are individually actionable and most want their own PR —
several touch risk-gated paths and cannot be batched with drivable work.

### The one pattern behind most of it

Six of seven reviewers independently found the same shape: **the 2026-08-09 Bash→Python conversion
and the #246/#257/#258 moves relabelled code without moving what pointed at it, and every loose end
fails green.** Six dangling `driver/`-relative paths, none of which turn anything red — an
`is_file()` guard silently skips, `testpaths` exits 0 having run nothing, `docs_check` prints an
honest SKIP that `make check` then ignores, `run_swarm` prints an error where nothing invokes it.

This is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` § *"When you change something, ask what it just invalidated"*
describes, arriving at scale. The structural reason it keeps landing undetected: **`docs_check` only
sees `[text](target)` markdown links, and the skill cites everything in backticks.** Three greps —
over backticked paths, mode names, and label names — would have caught eleven of the sixteen
falsified skill references below.

## Already fixed

On branch `chore/docs-archive-and-build-paths` (not yet PR'd):

- GitHub App private key moved out of the repo root to `~/.config/agent-session/`, `.env` repointed,
  and the `*.private-key.pem` ignore rule committed. It had existed only as an unstaged working-tree
  edit. The key was never committed — verified across every reachable git object.
- 26 pre-2026-08-09 dev-sessions archived to `docs/archive/dev-sessions/` via a new
  `scripts/archive-dev-session.py`. Tracked files under `docs/dev-sessions/` went 326 → 21.
- `pyproject.toml`: `testpaths` repaired (see S3), `pythonpath = ["src"]` added, dead ruff
  per-file-ignores removed, ruff `exclude` extended to `docs/archive`.

---

# Safety

## S1. The merge prohibition has no guard on the REST merge endpoint for the default backend

The complete effective Claude policy at the `Popen` boundary, printed from shipping code:

```
ALLOWED: Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Task,TodoWrite,BashOutput,KillShell,NotebookEdit,Bash(*)
DENIED : Bash(gh pr merge:*), Bash(gh pr merge *), Bash(git push --force:*),
         Bash(gh repo delete:*), Edit/Write/NotebookEdit(<skill_dir>/**)
```

`Bash(*)` is allowed and four patterns are denied. `gh api --method PUT /repos/o/r/pulls/N/merge`
and the `curl` equivalent are **not** among them. `OPENCODE_DENIED_COMMANDS`
(`src/agent_sessions/driver/agent_runner.py:62-63`) *does* deny both, so the non-default backend is
the better-defended one. `git push -f` (short form) is denied on neither — `BASE_DENIED_TOOLS`
spells only `git push --force`.

The only layer that ever covered those vectors is the PreToolUse hook — see S2.

**Fix:** add `gh api *pulls/*/merge*`, `curl *pulls/*/merge*`, and the `-f` short form to
`BASE_DENIED_TOOLS` so Claude's floor matches OpenCode's rather than depending on a hook.
**Tier:** `needs-review` — authorization work on a gated shipping path.

## S2. The PreToolUse merge-block hook has not been installed since the Python conversion

`src/agent_sessions/driver/lifecycle.py:374-375` resolves the hook assets next to itself:

```python
hook_settings_template = Path(__file__).parent / "settings.json"
hook_script = Path(__file__).parent / "merge-block-hook.sh"
```

`src/agent_sessions/driver/` contains only `.py` files; both assets live in repo-root `driver/` and
always have. So `hook_settings_template.is_file()` is False, `state_dir/settings.json` is never
written, and `lifecycle.py:930` passes `--settings <nonexistent path>` to the agent anyway.
`src/agent_sessions/scripts/backend_permission_probe.py:37-38` resolves the same two files
correctly via `PROJECT_ROOT / "driver"`, which is what makes this an oversight rather than a
decision.

Evidence it has been off since 2026-08-09: this repo's `.driver-state/settings.json` is dated Aug 6
— a pre-conversion leftover that happens to point at a real script, which is why nothing has been
observed to break locally. The decafclaw state dir's copy points at
`.worktrees/issue-170/driver/merge-block-hook.sh`, a worktree that no longer exists.

Why no test caught it:
- `tests/driver/test_driver_settings.py:12` asserts the string `--settings` appears in
  `lifecycle.py`'s **source text** — a presence-grep in Python clothing, satisfied by a comment.
  `assertion-lint` cannot see it because it matches only `grep -q`.
- `tests/driver/test_driver_settings.py:26-33` shells out to `jq` and asserts that **jq's assignment
  operator works**. The shipping code renders with `json.loads`/`dumps`. Nothing here calls
  `preflight`.
- `tests/driver/test_merge_hook.py:7` runs the launcher's copy of the script, not the path the
  shipping code resolves.
- `make driver-check` greps only the 8-line compatibility launcher (already tracked by #248).

**Fix:** move the two assets into the package (and ship them as package data), or point
`lifecycle.py` at `PROJECT_ROOT / "driver"` to match the probe. Then **drop the `if ... is_file()`
guard or make the miss loud** — a safety control that silently skips itself when its asset is
missing is the bug behind the bug. Replace the two tests with one that calls `preflight` and asserts
the rendered settings file exists and its `command` points at an executable file.
**Tier:** `needs-review` — gated coordinator, and it is a safety boundary.

## S3. A bare `pytest` reported success having run nothing *(fixed, recorded for the class)*

`pyproject.toml` still read `testpaths = ["driver", "scripts"]` after #257/#258 moved the suites;
both directories now hold only shell assets. `uv run pytest` collected zero tests and **exited 0**.
`make gate-test` passes explicit globs, so CI stayed honest and only the default was a false green.

Fixed on the branch above. Recorded because the class is the point: the relocation commits did not
carry `pyproject.toml`, and no check compares the two. **A guard asserting that a bare `pytest`
collects a non-zero count would close it** — `tests/scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py` already does
exactly that derivation for `make gate-test`, and its globs *were* updated.

## S4. `docs_check`'s assertion-count verification is permanently skipping — second cause

Distinct from #249, which owns the unexpanded-glob half. `src/agent_sessions/scripts/docs_check.py:175`
also passes `scripts/test_*.py`, a path that no longer contains Python. Fixing only the shell
expansion leaves that resolving to nothing, pytest exits 4, `returncode not in (0, 5)` returns
`None`, and the check stays a permanent SKIP. **Both causes have to change**; worth adding to #249
rather than filing separately.

---

# Correctness

## C1. `label_manager` still carries in three commands the bug its own test file documents as fixed

`removable()` (`src/agent_sessions/scripts/label_manager.py:42`) exists because
`gh issue edit --remove-label X` **errors when the repo has no label X at all**, failing the whole
edit including the add. Three commands route through it (`:139`, `:146`, `:169`); three build the
list unconditionally:

- `:115` `cmd_spec`
- `:163` `cmd_attempt`
- `:180` `cmd_merge_ready`

Two of the three survivors are on live paths, both inside `except Exception: pass`:
`src/agent_sessions/driver/parking.py:82` (`attempt --count`) and `parking.py:369`
(`merge-ready`, the `gate-eligible` success path). **On a fresh target repo the attempt label never
lands, the counter never increments, and the loop breaker cannot stop the loop.**

`tests/scripts/test_label_manager.py:1-17` states the diagnosis exactly — *"There were no tests here
at all before this file, which is why three commands carried the same bug"* — then tests only the
three that got the fix. `FakeGh` already reproduces the real `gh` behaviour, so the missing tests are
cheap. **Tier:** `needs-review` (gated `src/**`).

## C2. `make evidence` reads an abandoned state directory

`src/agent_sessions/scripts/evidence.py:34` hardcodes `state_dir = Path(".driver-state")`. The driver
writes to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/agent-session/<repo>/`
(`lifecycle.py:298-306`). Measured: `.driver-state/runs.jsonl` = 38 rows, last written 2026-08-06;
the live ledgers hold 318 real rows. `phase` — the module's primary grouping key — appears in none of
the stale rows, which is why every PHASE cell prints `unknown` today.

This matters more than a normal stale path: `docs_check.check_world_state_claims`
(`docs_check.py:326-329`) fails any bare count in the docs with *"use `make evidence` instead"*. The
doc-rot detector's prescribed remedy is reporting dead data, and `design.md:382` and
`orientation.md:350` both cite it as *"the only authoritative source for what has actually run."*

**Ordering constraint — do C3 first.** The live ledger currently contains ~1700 fabricated
`owner/repo` rows from the test suite, so repointing `evidence.py` before fixing test isolation
launders fixture data into the evidence report. **Tier:** `needs-review`.

## C3. The test suite writes into the operator's real `$HOME`; there is no `conftest.py`

There is **no `conftest.py` anywhere in the repo**, so nothing pins `XDG_STATE_HOME`. The fixture
repo `owner/repo` (`tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:64`) therefore resolves to a real path:

```
~/.local/state/agent-session/owner-repo/    11M, 872 run dirs, runs.jsonl ≈ 1700 rows
                                            plus inbox.md, parked.jsonl, workspaces/
```

Some suites do redirect individually (`tests/scripts/test_run_progress.py:177`,
`tests/driver/test_driver.py:465`); `test_full_loop.py` does not. Consequences: unbounded growth in
`$HOME`, non-hermetic tests that can read state left by earlier runs, and the C2 ordering problem.
The untracked `.local/` directory in the repo root is spill from the same non-hermeticity — benign
today (`gh` device-id), but the same misdirected `HOME` would equally write `gh`'s `hosts.yml`, which
holds OAuth tokens, into an unignored directory.

**Fix:** an autouse session fixture in a new `tests/conftest.py` pinning `XDG_STATE_HOME` to
`tmp_path`; delete `~/.local/state/agent-session/owner-repo/`; add `.local/` and `runs/` to
`.gitignore`. **Tier:** `auto-ok` — `tests/**` is drivable and the check is mechanical.

## C4. The full-loop suite's lock-isolation is inert, and the leak fires real `git push` at exit

`tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:735-737`:

```python
# The driver releases its lock from an atexit hook keyed on this global.
# monkeypatch restores it to None, so no pass can leave a live lock behind.
monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE", None)
```

The comment is wrong. `agent_session_driver.py:48` does `from ...locks import CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE`,
binding a **copy** of a `str | None`; `locks.release_lock`/`acquire_lock` read and write
`locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` via `global`. Nothing in `src/` reads the re-exported name. Demonstrated:
patching the barrel leaves `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` untouched.

Observable on every suite run — these are the `atexit` hook firing at worker shutdown, *after*
monkeypatch has restored the real `subprocess.run`:

```
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #102...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #101...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #109...
```

Harmless today only because the `tmp_path` repos have no `origin`. A test that ever pointed
`--repo-path` at a real checkout would push a ref deletion to a real remote from a test process.

**Fix:** patch `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` (the owning module) or add `locks.reset()`; add an autouse
teardown asserting it is `None`; drop `CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` from the barrel's re-exports so nobody
re-derives the wrong seam. **Tier:** `auto-ok` for the test half.

## C5. `gate.extract_gate` and `gate.budget_reclass` are tested but unreachable from a run

- `lifecycle.py:485` and `:1072` both call `gate.classify(pr_body, ...)`. `extract_gate` is called
  only from `gate.py`'s own CLI and from `tests/driver/test_gate.py` (~15 sites, always as
  `classify(extract_gate(body))`). So the tests exercise `extract_gate → classify` while production
  runs `classify(whole_body)`. `has_gate = bool(body.strip())` is then true for any non-empty PR
  body, and `gate_fields()` (`gate.py:186`) harvests every `key: value` line anywhere in it. It
  mostly still lands on `no-gate` via `validate_gate_block`, which is why it hasn't bitten — but the
  tested path and the run path differ **at the oracle**.
- `lifecycle.py:1084-1086` reimplements the budget rule inline while `gate.budget_reclass()`
  (`gate.py:592-604`) — with `_NO_VERDICT_OUTCOMES` and a 9-line docstring recording why the
  threshold is 95% — is referenced only from `gate.py`'s CLI and `test_gate.py:237`. The tested,
  documented implementation is unreachable; the live one is an untested literal.

**Fix:** call `gate.classify(gate.extract_gate(pr_body), ...)` at both sites (with a fixture proving
before/after on a real PR body), and replace the inline threshold with `gate.budget_reclass(...)`.
Note the second **moves** a threshold out of the coordinator into gated `gate.py` — a tightening,
not a widening, but say so in the PR. **Tier:** `needs-review` — the oracle.

## C6. Two skill phase files write label names the harness has never heard of

`skills/agent-session/phases/triage.md`:
- `:59`, `:95` — records `agent-session:needs-details`. `rg 'needs-details' src/` returns nothing.
- `:97` — records `agent-session:interactive`. The real name is
  `agent-session:needs-human-interactive` (`label_manager.py:16`, `parking.py:14`).

`src/agent_sessions/driver/writes.py:295` executes a `label` entry as one
`gh issue edit --add-label A --add-label B` with no ensure-exists, and `gh` errors when the repo has
no such label — so **the whole edit fails and the issue is never parked**, and
`write-manifest.md:43` then stops the rest of the manifest. `:97` compounds it with *"instead"*,
which leaves the issue carrying **no** park label, so the router keeps re-selecting it.
`intake.md:81` gets this right by emitting a `label_create` first; `triage.md` never does.

**Tier:** `needs-review` — `skills/**` is hard-gated.

## C7. Three scripts carry a repo-root derivation that is wrong post-src-layout

| site | expression | resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| `guard_lint.py:19` | `.parent.parent` | `src/agent_sessions` (unused, harmless) |
| `session_artifact_stats.py:16` | `.parent.parent` | `src/agent_sessions` (load-bearing) |
| `run_swarm.py:21` | `SCRIPTS_DIR.parent` | `src/agent_sessions` (load-bearing) |

Correct is `parents[3]`, as in `docs_check.py:44`, `assertion_lint.py:66`, `state_diagram.py:21`,
`backend_permission_probe.py:15`. Verified live:

```
$ uv run python -m agent_sessions.scripts.session_artifact_stats
Error: .../src/agent_sessions/docs/dev-sessions does not exist        exit=1
```

`run_swarm.py:59` additionally looks for `ROOT_DIR / "driver" / "agent_runner.py"`, deleted by the
conversion, and aborts every time. Its only reference is
`skills/agent-session/phases/execute.md:49`, which invokes the equally-gone
`python3 scripts/run_swarm.py`. **Both `run_swarm.py` and `session_artifact_stats.py` are
unreachable through any current entry point and broken if reached** — deleting them (plus the
`execute.md` reference, a gated skill edit) is a smaller change than fixing them. If `run_swarm`
goes, `validate_tdd.py` goes with it, and C8 becomes moot.

## C8. `validate_tdd` grades a stream it never read as compliant

`src/agent_sessions/scripts/validate_tdd.py:13-14` returns `True` for a missing stream, and
`run_swarm.py:114` double-guards the same null in the same unsafe direction
(`validate_stream(raw) if raw.exists() else True`). A subagent that crashed before writing anything
passes the TDD discipline check twice over. `tests/scripts/test_validate_tdd.py:98-100` enshrines
the fail-open, and `tests/scripts/test_run_swarm.py:25-45` never writes a stream, so
`assert data["passed"] is True` would hold with `validate_stream` deleted from the module.
Also `:65` treats any Bash output containing `FAIL` as a failing check, so `--tb=no` output
mentioning `FAILURES` satisfies the red phase.

Distinct from #249: there the check says it skipped; here it returns a **positive** and nothing
records that no evidence was examined. **Policy call for a human** — tri-state, or delete with C7.

## C9. `label_manager.get_current_labels` swallows every failure, so the transition guard permits

`src/agent_sessions/scripts/label_manager.py:69-76` returns `[]` on any exception. `main():229` feeds
that to `validate_transition():83`, which computes `is_parked = PARK_LABEL in current_labels`. A
transient rate-limit, auth or network failure therefore yields `is_parked = False` and a **parked
issue gets re-specced or re-attempted**. `board_audit.run_gh` (`:57-59`) raises on any nonzero exit;
the package already knows the right shape. Same file, `ensure_label_exists:36-39` swallows
`RuntimeError` unconditionally, making a 403 indistinguishable from "already exists".

## C10. `make guard-lint` scans at most 30 issues and reports a clean bill

`Makefile:145` pipes `gh issue list --json body` with no `--limit`; `gh`'s default is 30. On a repo
with more open issues the detector examines the newest 30 and prints *"no pinned test count guards
found"* — a null rendering as a positive, in a repo whose thesis is that this must not happen.
`board_audit` already solved it with `--limit 500` plus `bounded_records` raising at the limit.
`guard_lint` has no idea how many records it was handed. Not in `make check`, hence the rank.

## C11. `test_docs_check.py` clones the detector instead of calling it, and the clone has drifted

`tests/scripts/test_docs_check.py:62-100` reimplements `docs_check.check_world_state_claims` as a
local `check_line()` and asserts against the copy; `docs_check` is never called. Proven drift:

```
'Runs against many repositories'   test-copy: ['many repositories']  shipped-regex: False
```

The shipped pattern is `\b(one|two|…|ten|\d+) repositories\b`; the copy is `\b([a-z]+) repositories\b`.
The copy also carries an exemption the shipped code lacks and omits two the shipped code has, and
the shipped table's 2-tuples make the `cond = item[2:]` predicate path at `docs_check.py:369-374`
permanently dead — the mechanism exists only in the test. **`check_world_state_claims` — the newest
docs-check rule — has zero coverage through shipping code.** Delete `check_line` and the suite stays
green. This is defect class 1 instance 9 verbatim, inside the doc-rot detector's own suite, and it is
the residual risk `CLAUDE.md` names about leaving `tests/**` drivable.

`mypy src tests` (as opposed to the `mypy src` that `make typecheck` runs) flags this file at
`:84-86` with `"str" not callable`, which is the same defect surfacing as a type error.

---

# Structural

## T1. `agent_session_driver.py` is a re-export barrel that the package calls back through

143 lines that **define nothing** — an import list plus a 58-entry `__all__` and
`if __name__ == "__main__"`. Its `__all__` re-exports the standard library (`"datetime"`,
`"timezone"`) to serve **one line**: `tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:734` freezing time via
`monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "datetime", FrozenDatetime)`. To make that reachable,
`lifecycle.log()` and `locks.log()` each do a function-local import of the barrel purely to fetch
`agent_session_driver.datetime`.

`lifecycle.py` calls back through the barrel **44 times**, including `agent_session_driver.whoami` at
`:270` for a function defined at `lifecycle.py:146` — lifecycle calling itself via a module that
imports it. The cycle survives only because four modules defer their imports into function bodies
(14 sites across `lifecycle`, `board`, `parking`, `locks`). `board.say()` reaches the barrel, which
re-exports `lifecycle.say`, to write one line to stdout — while `lifecycle`, `parking` and
`pr_checks` define a **second, divergent** `say` that writes to stdout directly, so output behaviour
depends on which module you are in. Five spellings of one output helper set (four `say`, two `log`,
two `die`).

Read: **#246's decomposition is half-landed.** It extracted `RunContext` and named the lifecycle
operations, but kept the old god-module as a compatibility barrel so existing tests would not need
rewriting — and the modules now reach back through it. The seams were named without being cut. C4 is
the first concrete cost.

`agent_session_driver.py:14` also carries `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))`, a
pre-package fossil that puts the package directory on `sys.path`, making `board`, `locks`, `gate`,
`router`, `credentials` importable as top-level names. Nothing needs it.

**Fix, smallest first:** a tiny `driver/output.py` (`say`/`log`/`die`, no driver imports) that all
six modules import — this alone breaks three of `board.py`'s four barrel dependencies. Then move the
time seam to the owning module and delete the barrel's stdlib re-exports. Do **not** attempt full
de-shimming as unattended work. Distinct from #247, which is about the *GitHub I/O* surface; this is
the intra-package call graph. **Tier:** `needs-review` — gated file.

## T2. The lifecycle operations were named but not decomposed

`invoke_agent` 286 lines, `preflight` 230, `classify_and_record` 186, `select_queue` 162; and
`router.select` is a single 222-line function. The four-function shape from #246 is sound and I am
not proposing more than two extractions, each with an obvious seam:

- `lifecycle.py:700-813` — three independent GitHub reads appending to one `extra_context` string →
  `gather_extra_context(ctx, issue_num, phase, open_prs) -> str`
- `lifecycle.py:849-899` — the whole deterministic `request_review` branch → `run_request_review(...)`

That is ~170 of `invoke_agent`'s 286 lines, both testable in isolation. `preflight`'s inflight/orphan
warning (`:343-369`) and hook-settings block (`:371-385`) come out cleanly too.

## T3. Duplication worth collapsing

- **`gate.py:252-303` vs `:306-403`** — `verify_gate_rows` and `infer_provenance` encode the same
  seven row predicates twice, line for line, differing only in what they emit. Change a rule in one
  and the verdict disagrees with its own provenance record, **on the oracle**. Fix: one
  `_row_state(field, value)` per row consumed by both. `test_gate.py` already covers both.
- **`router.py:63-101` vs `lifecycle.py:521-555`** — `board_nums`, the priority-label filter,
  `is_specced`, and `candidates_json`/`markerless_json` are each computed twice. `router.py:85-90`
  reimplements `parking.is_specced` with inlined literals while `parking.py:16-17` defines
  `SPEC_LABEL`/`MARKER`, and `router.py:16-17` shadows `parking.py`'s `PARK_LABEL`/`MERGE_READY_LABEL`.
  **A label rename now needs four edits and fails open** (issues silently stop being selected).
  Label constants are triplicated across `label_manager.py:12-22`, `parking.py:13-16`,
  `router.py:16-17`.
- **`parking.py:60-68, 73-81, 88-99, 103-111, 115-123, 369-377`** — six copies of the same seven-line
  `label_manager.py` subprocess block, four of which discard the failure entirely. `label_manager`
  exposes an importable `main(argv) -> int`; a typed call returning 1 is hard to ignore, a swallowed
  `CalledProcessError` is the default. This is *why* C1 and C9 are invisible.
- **`parking.py:126-268`** — `has_new_human_comment` implements the same comment/reaction scan twice
  (GraphQL and REST branches) with four copies of the same timestamp-normalisation triple-replace, in
  one 143-line function. Extraction takes it to ~60 lines.
- **`lifecycle.py:462-490` vs `:1044-1080`** — `run_classify_only` duplicates the tail of
  `classify_and_record`; the recovery path and the normal path can drift, and per C5 they already
  differ from the tested path together.
- **Three incompatible `gh` wrappers** — `board_audit.run_gh:49` (raises, decodes JSON),
  `label_manager.run_gh:25` (raises `RuntimeError`, returns text), `doctor._gh:88` (injects tokens,
  returns raw `CompletedProcess`, never checks `returncode` — callers use
  `getattr(res, "returncode", 1)` at eleven sites). They differ on the three things that matter:
  token injection, error propagation, truncation. Lower priority than the correctness items: the
  divergences are mostly deliberate.
- **Four JSONL readers, four tolerance policies** — `run_progress.read_records:87-114` is the good
  one and documents why; `evidence.py:42-50`, `validate_tdd.py:17-25`, and
  `backend_permission_probe.observed_denials:69-74` each re-derive it worse. The last calls `.get`
  on records `json.loads` may have returned as `str` or `int`.

## T4. Dead code left by the conversion and the #246 split

- `SelectionResult.board_items` / `.open_issues` (`lifecycle.py:74-75`) — populated at `:661-662`,
  read by nobody.
- `InvocationResult.writes_file` / `.run_repo_path` (`lifecycle.py:88,96`) — set at `:955,962`, never
  read.
- `parking.clear_attempt_labels` (`:59`) — referenced only by the barrel's import and `__all__`.
- `router.py:106` declares `p4_escalate` and **never appends to it**; `:210` concatenates an
  always-empty list. `design.md:340` documents P4 as a real priority.
- `agent_runner.py:21-28` — an `ImportError` fallback that re-imports the module from the same
  package path that just failed, for a `python agent_runner.py` invocation nothing performs.
- `agent_runner.py:565` — `_main(argv)` never touches `argv`; the body reads `sys.argv`.
- `discussion_manager.py:76` — unused `emoji` parameter, and a "Deprecated alias" docstring on what
  is now the supported entry point (via `scripts/bootstrap-repo.sh:56`).
- `Makefile:41` — `.PHONY: ... driver-test-sh` names a target with **no rule anywhere**. It exists in
  the target database only because `.PHONY` names it, and `make driver-test-sh` exits 0 having done
  nothing. Bash-era leftover.

## T5. `perform_writes` mutates the shape it returns

`pr_checks.py:193-195` bolts `messages`, `entries`, `applied` onto the dict `writes.execute` returned
(`writes.py:405`, keys `ok`/`errors`/`results`). Both are annotated bare `dict`, so mypy sees
`dict[Any, Any]` and `inv.writes_result["applied"]` (`lifecycle.py:988`) is unchecked. A `TypedDict`
per shape would catch a key typo. Minor: `RunContext.workspaces_dir: str` (`lifecycle.py:66`) is the
one path-shaped field typed `str` among nine `Path` neighbours, so both consumers repeat
`Path(ctx.workspaces_dir).resolve() if ... else None`.

## T6. `reconciler.py`'s webhook half has no host

`run_webhook_reconciler`, `parse_webhook_event`, `handle_event`, `handle_issue_comment`, and
`PollingAdapter.synthesize_comment_event` are referenced only within `reconciler.py` and its tests;
`.github/workflows/` has only `check.yml`. Production uses only `synthesize_pr_event` +
`handle_pr_reconcile`. **Keep it** — pure, cheap, tested, and named in `design.md` as the reactive
path — but `run_webhook_reconciler:278-279` should not claim `"acquired_git_lock": True` when it
acquires nothing.

---

# Tests

## X1. `assertion-lint` covers 15 of 33 test files, and would not have caught either real instance

`assertion_lint.py:81` sets `SCOPE = "tests/driver/test_*.py"`; all 18 files under `tests/scripts/`
are unlinted. Both S2's presence-grep and C11's cloned detector use Python `in` against
`read_text()`, not `grep -q`, so the linter would miss them even in scope. **Two things for a human:**
widening `SCOPE` to `tests/{driver,scripts}/test_*.py`, and adding a rule for
`assert <literal> in <source_text>` where the right-hand side came from reading a repo file. The
second is the pattern that actually bit. The docstring's own warning about false positives training
the operator to wave the check through is the reason this is a judgment call.

## X2. Two weak GitHub fakes sit beside the strong one

`tests/driver/test_workspace_driver_integration.py:52-65,122-126,185-192` and
`tests/driver/test_driver.py:445-457,487-508,542-552` monkeypatch `subprocess.run` with a catch-all
`MockResult` (`stdout = "{}"`, `returncode = 0`) that answers **every** unmodelled `gh` call with
success. `test_full_loop.py`'s docstring (lines 20-31) names this exact anti-pattern as the reason
`FakeGitHub.unhandled` and `field_gaps` exist. `test_workspace_driver_integration.py` would pass if
the driver started issuing a completely different set of GitHub calls. Plus `test_driver.py:433-601`
repeats ~25 lines of setup verbatim three times.

## X3. No `conftest.py`; the `sys.path` bootstrap is copy-pasted 24 times

`sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "src"))` appears in 24 files while nine
others import `agent_sessions` with no bootstrap, so the split is arbitrary. `pythonpath = ["src"]`
(landed on the branch above) makes all 24 deletable. `dummy_git_repo` is byte-identical in
`tests/driver/test_workspace.py:27-37` and `test_workspace_driver_integration.py:10-20`. Moving
`FakeGitHub`/`StubAgent`/`LoopHarness` into `tests/driver/conftest.py` is the prerequisite for fixing
X2.

## X4. Coverage gaps that matter

- **`--classify-only` has zero coverage.** The flag appears only in `lifecycle.py`. This is the
  branch an operator reaches for *after* a run dies mid-flight — `lifecycle.py:360-369` prints it as
  the recovery instruction three times.
- **`locks.py:120-152`'s stale-lock steal and TTL are untested.** No test references
  `force-with-lease`, `ttl`, or the steal path. Untested: `lock_age >= ttl_seconds` → force-with-lease
  push; the 600s/7200s split by phase (`locks.py:71`); a lease that *loses* the race; `release_lock`
  itself. This is the distributed mutual-exclusion primitive — get the TTL wrong and two drivers run
  the same issue, spending budget twice. `FakeGitHub.held_locks` already takes a timestamp, so the
  steal case is a one-line fixture change.

## X5. Slow, fragile, and CWD-dependent tests

- **One test is 85% of the wall clock.** `test_gate_test_wiring.py::test_new_test_file_runs_under_gate_test_with_no_makefile_edit`
  takes 30.3s of a 35.6s run because it invokes `make gate-test` twice for real — so `make check`
  runs the whole suite three times over. **Do not weaken it**; it is the only thing standing between
  you and a test file that silently never runs. Worth knowing the floor is ~3×, and worth an `-x` on
  the with-probe arm, which only needs to observe one failure.
- `xdist_group` at `test_gate_test_wiring.py:44` is **inert** — it is honoured only under
  `--dist loadgroup`, and `make gate-test` runs `-n auto` with no `--dist`. C1 and C2 can land on
  different workers and run concurrently while C2 writes a probe file into the tree C1 is collecting.
  Masked today by the process-unique probe name.
- No git-config isolation in any `git init` fixture: no `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, no
  `commit.gpgsign=false`. A developer or CI image with global `commit.gpgsign` or `core.hooksPath`
  breaks eight tests in a way that reads as a code failure.
- CWD-relative paths in `test_driver_settings.py:8,10,15,23,24`, `test_merge_hook.py:7,13,19,25,30`,
  `test_board_audit.py:443,563`, `test_gate.py:222,551`, while every other suite derives
  `parents[2]`. `test_driver_settings.py:9-10` silently falls back to a *different* file if
  `lifecycle.py` is missing, so a rename makes it grade the wrong artifact rather than fail. It also
  requires `jq` on `$PATH`.
- `test_evidence.py:27,40,46` replaces `builtins.open` and `Path.is_file` process-wide;
  `test_discussion_manager.py:16-17` builds expected titles from the real wall clock, so crossing UTC
  midnight between two calls fails the test.
- Vacuous: `test_writes.py:93` (`assert spec is not None` over `KINDS.items()`),
  `test_driver.py:527` (`isinstance(..., list)` immediately before a length assertion),
  `test_docs_check.py:36,52` (defensive `getattr` then `assert ... is not None`).

**On `test_full_loop.py`: I would argue against splitting it.** 1594 lines, but one harness, one
fake, one stub agent, and five explicitly labelled case groups whose seam is *the driver pass*, not a
module. Its assertions are whole-object equality on `runs.jsonl` rows and whole-list equality on
`label_ops`, and `LoopHarness.run` asserts `gh.unhandled == []` and `gh.field_gaps == []` on every
pass. Extract the harness to `conftest.py`; leave the bodies together.

---

comment.body:
## Progress — 2026-08-19, second pass

Five commits, stacked linearly on a `wip/261-base` that merges the two branches from the
previous pass. Nothing pushed, nothing PR'd. `make check` green on each.

| Branch (in stack order) | Closes |
|---|---|
| `fix/261-make-check-cold-venv` | **N1** (new) |
| `fix/261-is-shim-and-partition` | **G3**, **G2** |
| `fix/261-dead-scripts-and-guard-lint` | **C7**, **C10**, **C8**, **H9** (partial) |
| `fix/261-oracle-call-sites` | **C5**, **X4** |
| `fix/261-drivable-hygiene` | **C11**, **H1**, **H3**, **H7**, **X3**, **X5** |

### New findings, not in this issue

**N1. `make check` fails on a cold `.venv`, deterministically.** Found on the first
`make check` of the branch these commits sit on:

```
$ rm -rf .venv && make check
error: Failed to install: ruff-0.16.2-py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl (ruff==0.16.2)
make[1]: *** [commit-lint] Error 2
```

Seven jobs run under `$(MAKE) -j check-parallel` and each enters through `uv run`, which
populates `.venv` on demand. They race; one loses. Every fresh worktree hits it. The
message names a wheel, so it reads as a network fault — and rerunning succeeds, because
the venv is warm by then. That trains the operator to treat the project's only aggregate
gate as flaky. Fixed with a `venv` target reached from `check`'s recipe.

**N2. `run_classify_only` prints "recorded to runs.jsonl" and records nothing.** Only
`classify_and_record` opens `ctx.runs_log`. Park state *is* applied — so an operator
completing a dead run's bookkeeping gets the issue parked, is told the ledger was
written, and `runs.jsonl` has no row for the run that parked it. Surfaced by X4's new
coverage. **This is a decision for you**, not a defect with an obvious repair: the
recovery path has cost, session, ts, outcome and reason in hand but not `phase` or
`exit`. The new check asserts the *discrepancy* rather than either half, so whichever way
you settle it, that test is the one that changes and the diff says which was chosen.

**N3. `make guard-lint` can only ever grade the repo you are standing in.** The recipe is
a bare `gh issue list` with no `--repo`, while every other live target takes `$(REPO)`.
Left alone — changing which repo a check grades is your call — but it means C10's fix
bounds the scan without widening it to the repo #68 was written about.

### C5 is worse than this issue records it

The issue says the divergence "mostly still lands on `no-gate` … which is why it hasn't
bitten." It is reachable on entirely valid data, and it fails **permissive**:

```
gate block:      verdict: human-merge-required
summary above:   "The run before this recorded  verdict: eligible-for-auto-merge"

whole body (production)   verdict='eligible-for-auto-merge'   outcome='gate-eligible'
extracted (tested)        verdict='human-merge-required'      outcome='gate-human'
```

`gate_fields` harvests every `^key: value` line it is handed and the first occurrence
wins, and an ordinary PR summary sits above the gate block. A run whose own gate block
asked for a human was classified eligible for auto-merge. Those outcomes route
oppositely — one labels the PR merge-ready, the other parks the issue.

Scanned 240 real PRs across both repos: **8 already classify differently** under the two
paths. None flips outcome today (they differ in harvested fields, reason text, and the
recorded artifact), so this is a latent defect closed rather than an incident cleaned up.

`gate.yaml` was affected too — on decafclaw #847 it recorded 2167 bytes of PR summary
where a 305-byte block belongs.

One existing assertion changed, and it is worth flagging that it is not a weakening:
`test_pass_ending_gate_eligible` pinned `gate.yaml == the whole PR body` with the comment
*"Pinned as behaviour; #184 is the fix."* **#184 landed the schema validation and closed
without touching the extraction**, so a golden was holding the defect in place with a
pointer to an issue that had gone. `gate_body`'s docstring carried the same stale
deferral.

The budget half had drifted too: the inline copy lacked `budget_reclass`'s `budget > 0`
guard, so under `--max-budget-usd 0` a run that spent nothing became `budget-exhausted`
— an outcome that *stops the loop*. Verified by reverting: the test fails with
*"stopping the loop: outcome means an assumption is wrong."*

### G3 — `is_shim` was wrong in both directions

Not just too narrow. The old predicate (a marker string, or under 30 lines mentioning
`from agent_sessions`) missed the facade it was written for **and** matched ordinary short
modules that import one helper and define one function. Length was never the property
that mattered; originating nothing is. It is now an AST question.

The rule around it also got more precise rather than merely stricter. Naming a facade is
not itself the defect — an entry point is worth gating even after it thins out, which is
exactly why the compatibility launcher is gated. The defect is a facade standing in *for*
the implementation. So it fails only when *none* of the modules a facade re-exports from
is named in the section. Any, not all: the real facade re-exports from five modules,
unlisted paths are `needs-review` by default so their absence exposes nothing, and
demanding a bullet each would fill the section with entries carrying no reason.

Per your call, `lifecycle.py` is now named explicitly and the facade keeps its own bullet
with the launcher's reason. Both governance files edited identically and still
byte-identical.

### Things this issue got right that were worth re-verifying, and one figure that has moved

- **X5's eight tests is exactly eight.** Pointing `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` at a two-line
  config with `commit.gpgsign = true` breaks precisely the eight named, and they arrive as
  `CalledProcessError` from a `git commit` a *fixture* ran — so it reads as the code under
  test being broken.
- **C11's drift is exactly as described**, and it produced three of H3's four hidden mypy
  errors.
- **C10's truncation was latent here, not active.** 21 open issues against `gh`'s default
  30. Against decafclaw — 141 open issues, and the repo #68 was written about — the old
  command saw 30 of 141.
- **X5's "30.3s of a 35.6s run" is now 8.86s of 11.5s.** Still the single slowest test,
  still worth its cost, deliberately not weakened.

### Two places my own controls caught my own fix

Recording these because they are the argument for writing the control alongside the check.

- **H1.** The obvious fix, `$(or $(ISSUES),$(LOOP_ISSUES))`, is wrong: `ISSUES ?= 1`
  means `$(ISSUES)` is never empty, so `$(or)` cannot tell "the caller asked" from "the
  file defaulted", and a bare `make loop` collapsed to one issue. C2 caught it.
  `$(origin)` distinguishes them.
- **X5's git isolation.** The first attempt was `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` plus
  `GIT_AUTHOR_*`. Those variables outrank *repo-level* config, so it silently re-authored
  the commits in the two fixtures that set their own — passing suites, wrong authorship,
  nothing to say so. A stub global config file sits below repo config, which is the
  ordering the fixtures were written against.

### Still open

- The gated `skills/**` edit dropping `execute.md`'s `run_swarm` references, staged
  separately per your instruction. Plus K1–K8.
- `findings.md:1032` cites `session_artifact_stats` as a runnable command; goes with D5.
- **S4** belongs on #249, not here — `docs_check`'s assertion-count probe passes
  `scripts/test_*.py`, a path with no Python, which is a *second* cause on top of that
  issue's unexpanded globs. Fixing only #249's half leaves the check permanently skipping.
- H2, H5, D2–D8, T2–T4, X2, D7, and the K9 / `AGENTS.md`-pointer decisions.

issue.title: Review: full-repo maintainability and documentation audit (2026-08-19)

labels.name: needs-review
labels.description: A human-judgment criterion or a risk-gated path

issue.body:
## Context

Full-repo maintainability and documentation review, 2026-08-19. Seven parallel reviewers over the
driver core, the scripts package, the test suites, `design.md`/`orientation.md`/`README.md`,
`usage.md`/`findings.md`/`prior-art.md`, `skills/**` plus `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, and build/CI/repo
hygiene. Every claim below was re-verified against the code by hand before landing here; findings
that did not survive verification were dropped.

This issue is the capture record. Items are individually actionable and most want their own PR —
several touch risk-gated paths and cannot be batched with drivable work.

### The one pattern behind most of it

Six of seven reviewers independently found the same shape: **the 2026-08-09 Bash→Python conversion
and the #246/#257/#258 moves relabelled code without moving what pointed at it, and every loose end
fails green.** Six dangling `driver/`-relative paths, none of which turn anything red — an
`is_file()` guard silently skips, `testpaths` exits 0 having run nothing, `docs_check` prints an
honest SKIP that `make check` then ignores, `run_swarm` prints an error where nothing invokes it.

This is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` § *"When you change something, ask what it just invalidated"*
describes, arriving at scale. The structural reason it keeps landing undetected: **`docs_check` only
sees `[text](target)` markdown links, and the skill cites everything in backticks.** Three greps —
over backticked paths, mode names, and label names — would have caught eleven of the sixteen
falsified skill references below.

## Already fixed

On branch `chore/docs-archive-and-build-paths` (not yet PR'd):

- GitHub App private key moved out of the repo root to `~/.config/agent-session/`, `.env` repointed,
  and the `*.private-key.pem` ignore rule committed. It had existed only as an unstaged working-tree
  edit. The key was never committed — verified across every reachable git object.
- 26 pre-2026-08-09 dev-sessions archived to `docs/archive/dev-sessions/` via a new
  `scripts/archive-dev-session.py`. Tracked files under `docs/dev-sessions/` went 326 → 21.
- `pyproject.toml`: `testpaths` repaired (see S3), `pythonpath = ["src"]` added, dead ruff
  per-file-ignores removed, ruff `exclude` extended to `docs/archive`.

---

# Safety

## S1. The merge prohibition has no guard on the REST merge endpoint for the default backend

The complete effective Claude policy at the `Popen` boundary, printed from shipping code:

```
ALLOWED: Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Task,TodoWrite,BashOutput,KillShell,NotebookEdit,Bash(*)
DENIED : Bash(gh pr merge:*), Bash(gh pr merge *), Bash(git push --force:*),
         Bash(gh repo delete:*), Edit/Write/NotebookEdit(<skill_dir>/**)
```

`Bash(*)` is allowed and four patterns are denied. `gh api --method PUT /repos/o/r/pulls/N/merge`
and the `curl` equivalent are **not** among them. `OPENCODE_DENIED_COMMANDS`
(`src/agent_sessions/driver/agent_runner.py:62-63`) *does* deny both, so the non-default backend is
the better-defended one. `git push -f` (short form) is denied on neither — `BASE_DENIED_TOOLS`
spells only `git push --force`.

The only layer that ever covered those vectors is the PreToolUse hook — see S2.

**Fix:** add `gh api *pulls/*/merge*`, `curl *pulls/*/merge*`, and the `-f` short form to
`BASE_DENIED_TOOLS` so Claude's floor matches OpenCode's rather than depending on a hook.
**Tier:** `needs-review` — authorization work on a gated shipping path.

## S2. The PreToolUse merge-block hook has not been installed since the Python conversion

`src/agent_sessions/driver/lifecycle.py:374-375` resolves the hook assets next to itself:

```python
hook_settings_template = Path(__file__).parent / "settings.json"
hook_script = Path(__file__).parent / "merge-block-hook.sh"
```

`src/agent_sessions/driver/` contains only `.py` files; both assets live in repo-root `driver/` and
always have. So `hook_settings_template.is_file()` is False, `state_dir/settings.json` is never
written, and `lifecycle.py:930` passes `--settings <nonexistent path>` to the agent anyway.

## C4. The full-loop suite's lock-isolation is inert, and the leak fires real `git push` at exit

`tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:735-737`:

```python
# The driver releases its lock from an atexit hook keyed on this global.
# monkeypatch restores it to None, so no pass can leave a live lock behind.
monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE", None)
```

The comment is wrong. `agent_session_driver.py:48` does `from ...locks import CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE`,
binding a **copy** of a `str | None`; `locks.release_lock`/`acquire_lock` read and write
`locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` via `global`. Nothing in `src/` reads the re-exported name. Demonstrated:
patching the barrel leaves `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` untouched.

Observable on every suite run — these are the `atexit` hook firing at worker shutdown, *after*
monkeypatch has restored the real `subprocess.run`:

```
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #102...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #101...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #109...
```

Harmless today only because the `tmp_path` repos have no `origin`. A test that ever pointed
`--repo-path` at a real checkout would push a ref deletion to a real remote from a test process.

**Fix:** patch `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` (the owning module) or add `locks.reset()`; add an autouse
teardown asserting it is `None`; drop `CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` from the barrel's re-exports so nobody
re-derives the wrong seam. **Tier:** `auto-ok` for the test half.

# Structural

## T1. `agent_session_driver.py` is a re-export barrel that the package calls back through

143 lines that **define nothing** — an import list plus a 58-entry `__all__` and
`if __name__ == "__main__"`. Its `__all__` re-exports the standard library (`"datetime"`,
`"timezone"`) to serve **one line**: `tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:734` freezing time via
`monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "datetime", FrozenDatetime)`. To make that reachable,
`lifecycle.log()` and `locks.log()` each do a function-local import of the barrel purely to fetch
`agent_session_driver.datetime`.

`lifecycle.py` calls back through the barrel **44 times**, including `agent_session_driver.whoami` at
`:270` for a function defined at `lifecycle.py:146` — lifecycle calling itself via a module that
imports it. The cycle survives only because four modules defer their imports into function bodies
(14 sites across `lifecycle`, `board`, `parking`, `locks`). `board.say()` reaches the barrel, which
re-exports `lifecycle.say`, to write one line to stdout — while `lifecycle`, `parking` and
`pr_checks` define a **second, divergent** `say` that writes to stdout directly, so output behaviour
depends on which module you are in. Five spellings of one output helper set (four `say`, two `log`,
two `die`).

Read: **#246's decomposition is half-landed.** It extracted `RunContext` and named the lifecycle
operations, but kept the old god-module as a compatibility barrel so existing tests would not need
rewriting — and the modules now reach back through it. The seams were named without being cut. C4 is
the first concrete cost.

`agent_session_driver.py:14` also carries `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))`, a
pre-package fossil that puts the package directory on `sys.path`, making `board`, `locks`, `gate`,
`router`, `credentials` importable as top-level names. Nothing needs it.

**Fix, smallest first:** a tiny `driver/output.py` (`say`/`log`/`die`, no driver imports) that all
six modules import — this alone breaks three of `board.py`'s four barrel dependencies. Then move the
time seam to the owning module and delete the barrel's stdlib re-exports. Do **not** attempt full
de-shimming as unattended work. Distinct from #247, which is about the *GitHub I/O* surface; this is
the intra-package call graph. **Tier:** `needs-review` — gated file.

## T2. The lifecycle operations were named but not decomposed

`invoke_agent` 286 lines, `preflight` 230, `classify_and_record` 186, `select_queue` 162; and
`router.select` is a single 222-line function. The four-function shape from #246 is sound and I am
not proposing more than two extractions, each with an obvious seam:

  the recovery instruction three times.
- **`locks.py:120-152`'s stale-lock steal and TTL are untested.** No test references
  `force-with-lease`, `ttl`, or the steal path. Untested: `lock_age >= ttl_seconds` → force-with-lease
  push; the 600s/7200s split by phase (`locks.py:71`); a lease that *loses* the race; `release_lock`
  itself. This is the distributed mutual-exclusion primitive — get the TTL wrong and two drivers run
  the same issue, spending budget twice. `FakeGitHub.held_locks` already takes a timestamp, so the
  steal case is a one-line fixture change.

## X5. Slow, fragile, and CWD-dependent tests

- **One test is 85% of the wall clock.** `test_gate_test_wiring.py::test_new_test_file_runs_under_gate_test_with_no_makefile_edit`
  takes 30.3s of a 35.6s run because it invokes `make gate-test` twice for real — so `make check`
  runs the whole suite three times over. **Do not weaken it**; it is the only thing standing between
  you and a test file that silently never runs. Worth knowing the floor is ~3×, and worth an `-x` on
  the with-probe arm, which only needs to observe one failure.
- `xdist_group` at `test_gate_test_wiring.py:44` is **inert** — it is honoured only under
  `--dist loadgroup`, and `make gate-test` runs `-n auto` with no `--dist`. C1 and C2 can land on
  different workers and run concurrently while C2 writes a probe file into the tree C1 is collecting.
  Masked today by the process-unique probe name.
- No git-config isolation in any `git init` fixture: no `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, no
  `commit.gpgsign=false`. A developer or CI image with global `commit.gpgsign` or `core.hooksPath`
  breaks eight tests in a way that reads as a code failure.
- CWD-relative paths in `test_driver_settings.py:8,10,15,23,24`, `test_merge_hook.py:7,13,19,25,30`,
  `test_board_audit.py:443,563`, `test_gate.py:222,551`, while every other suite derives
  `parents[2]`. `test_driver_settings.py:9-10` silently falls back to a *different* file if
  `lifecycle.py` is missing, so a rename makes it grade the wrong artifact rather than fail. It also
  requires `jq` on `$PATH`.
- `test_evidence.py:27,40,46` replaces `builtins.open` and `Path.is_file` process-wide;
  `test_discussion_manager.py:16-17` builds expected titles from the real wall clock, so crossing UTC
  midnight between two calls fails the test.
- Vacuous: `test_writes.py:93` (`assert spec is not None` over `KINDS.items()`),
  `test_driver.py:527` (`isinstance(..., list)` immediately before a length assertion),
  `test_docs_check.py:36,52` (defensive `getattr` then `assert ... is not None`).

**On `test_full_loop.py`: I would argue against splitting it.** 1594 lines, but one harness, one
fake, one stub agent, and five explicitly labelled case groups whose seam is *the driver pass*, not a
module. Its assertions are whole-object equality on `runs.jsonl` rows and whole-list equality on
`label_ops`, and `LoopHarness.run` asserts `gh.unhandled == []` and `gh.field_gaps == []` on every
pass. Extract the harness to `conftest.py`; leave the bodies together.

---

comment.body:
## Progress — 2026-08-19

Eight items landed across two branches, neither pushed. `make check` green on both;
they merge cleanly with each other (verified with `git merge-tree`), and the only file
they share is `docs/design.md`, in different regions.

### `chore/docs-archive-and-build-paths`

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `79f77e6` | **The private key.** `*.private-key.pem` was ignored only by an *unstaged* working-tree edit. Rule committed; key moved to `~/.config/agent-session/` and `.env` repointed. Never committed — verified across every reachable git object. |
| `8988e62` | 26 pre-rewrite dev-sessions archived; tracked files under `docs/dev-sessions/` 326 → 21. New `scripts/archive-dev-session.py`. |
| `e2f689a` | **S3.** `testpaths = ["tests"]`, so a bare `pytest` no longer exits 0 having run nothing. Plus `pythonpath = ["src"]`, dead ruff per-file-ignores removed, ruff `exclude` extended to `docs/archive`. |

### `fix/261-hook-and-permission-floor`

| Commit | Closes |
|---|---|
| `02cef0a` | **S1, S2**, part of D3, H4 |
| `c95278a` | **C3, C4** |
| `7b9aa52` | **C2**, H6, part of H10, part of T4, part of X5 |
| `e60adde` | **C1, C9** |
| `b3a24ab` | **D1**, part of D2 |
| `db770f4` | **G1** (partial), **D2** |
| `a278ede` | **T1** (partial), part of T4, part of D9 |

### Verified outcomes, not just "fixed"

- **The hook is installed again**, and fails closed when it cannot be. The three tests
  that covered it never touched the install path; replaced with tests that call
  `preflight` and assert the rendered file names an executable that exists, plus a
  control proving a missing template now stops the run. `driver/` is down to the
  compatibility launcher alone.
- **The suites no longer write to `$HOME`.** `~/.local/state/agent-session/owner-repo/`
  held 897 run dirs and 1748 ledger rows, all `repo: "owner/repo"`, still growing during
  the review. A full `make check` now adds **zero**. The directory is moved aside, not
  deleted, under `/tmp`.
- **`make evidence` reports real data** — 319 runs across both repos with real phase
  names, where every PHASE cell used to read `unknown`. This had to land *after* the
  isolation fix, or 1748 fixture rows would have become "evidence".
- **The lock leak is gone.** `Releasing lock for #N...` at pytest exit no longer happens.
- **All six `label_manager` remove-lists are narrowed.** Eight new tests fail with the
  exact production error before the change.

### Corrections to this issue's own text

- **G1, hunk 3.** I wrote that `codex` has no `-p`. It does: `-p` is
  `--profile <CONFIG_PROFILE_V2>`. So `Codex -p` would not have errored — it would have
  silently consumed the next token as a config profile name. Worse failure, same
  conclusion; non-interactive Codex is `codex exec`.
- **T1.** I described the barrel's `datetime` re-export as serving one test line. It was
  the driver's **single clock seam**, read by eight sites across five modules so one patch
  freezes time everywhere. A real function, badly housed — so the fix was to name the
  clock (`output.now()`), not just move the loggers. Function-local barrel imports went
  14-across-4-modules → 7-across-2.

### Still open, and why

- **G1 proper.** `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` are now byte-identical, which sharpens the
  question rather than settling it. Making `AGENTS.md` a pointer needs
  `docs_check.check_risk_policy_parity` taught the pointer shape, and it is a judgment
  about whether a Codex-hosted run needs its instruction file to stand alone.
- **S1, the REST merge patterns.** `git push -f` added to both backends. The
  `gh api`/`curl` merge-endpoint rules are deliberately *not* added as tool-level
  patterns: they would have to match mid-command, `--help` does not state whether the
  rule syntax supports that, and an unverified entry in a floor whose value is that it is
  verified is the wrong trade. The hook covers them, now tested per vector.
  `make backend-permission-probe BACKEND=claude` is the one live run that settles it.
- **K9** (the Ceremony Threshold, and `task: deny` on OpenCode) — both human decisions.
- Everything else in the ranked lists above.

labels.name: needs-review
