> Continued from the issue body — full-repo review, 2026-08-19.

# Skill (`skills/**` — all hard-gated)

## K1. Falsified references

- **`pr` is a mode with no phase file — 14 live references:** `SKILL.md:3` (frontmatter triggers),
  `:52`, `:84`; `express.md:9`; `execute.md:37`, `:105`; `plan.md:26`, `:30`; `grade_gate.md:130`;
  `frozen-checks.md:3`, `:129`, `:161`, `:188`, `:190`; `github-projects.md:4`, `:117`.
  `frozen-checks.md:130` and `:306` **were** updated to `grade_gate.md` while five other lines in the
  same file were not. `express.md:9` is the sharpest: it names three phase files to read in sequence
  and one does not exist.
- **The dispatcher omits two modes the driver actively requests.** `SKILL.md:22-33` lists ten;
  `phases/` holds twelve. Missing: `fix_conflict` (requested at `reconciler.py:75`) and `refine`
  (`router.py:188`). `pr_checks.py:231` tells the agent to read `SKILL.md` then the phase file, so it
  lands in a phase its own dispatcher denies exists. No orphans in the other direction.
- `execute.md:49`, `:53`, `:55` — pre-conversion `scripts/run_swarm.py` / `scripts/validate_tdd.py`
  paths (see C7).
- `execute.md:55` attributes `--tier low` to `agent_runner.py` (it is `run_swarm`'s own flag) and
  names *"Claude 3.5 Haiku"* as the low tier. No model name is hardcoded anywhere; the mapping comes
  from `--low-tier-model`/`LOW_TIER_MODEL`. An invented constant in a doc that forbids them.
- `grade_gate.md:97-99` asserts as *"Measured"* that a `sleep` poll loop and a backgrounded shell are
  *denied* under the permission floor. `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` includes `Bash(*)`, `BashOutput` **and**
  `KillShell`, so both are allowed; only `Monitor` is genuinely unavailable. The *advice*
  (`gh pr checks --watch`) is right; the stated reason is false.
- Stale step numbers from the split: `open_pr.md:96` cites "Step 14" in a 9-step file;
  `grade_gate.md:21` cites "step 12" in a 2-step file; `grade_gate.md:24` cites an unlabelled
  cross-phase "step 5"; `pr-body-template.md:79` cites "step 14". **Cite phases by name across a
  boundary.** Also `express.md:75` says *"2a–2i"* over a table running 2a–2g, and
  `documentarian-prompt.md:36` cites *"Three tests every check must pass"* — the heading is **Two**.
- `acceptance-criteria.md:167` — the flagship worked example in the file that *teaches tier
  derivation* cites **trigger 2** (risk-gated path) for what is **trigger 1** (a criterion resting on
  human judgment). Nothing in the example touches a risk path.

## K2. `rethink`'s "CRITICAL" un-spec step is a no-op in the common case

`rethink.md:26` says to replace the `<!-- agent-session:spec -->` marker with `spec-RETIRED`, warning
that otherwise the driver still sees the issue as specced. But `router.py:87-90`'s `is_specced`
returns true on the **label** *or* the comment, and `intake.md:85`/`triage.md:73` both apply the
**label** — so the label is the normal carrier and `rethink` never removes it.

## K3. `github-projects.md` instructs writes the agent cannot perform

`:96`, `:104-108` and the whole ID-resolution section tell the agent to run
`gh project item-add` / `item-edit` directly. The agent's credential is read-scoped; board moves go
through `project_item_add`/`project_item_edit` manifest entries (`writes.py:61-62`).
`session-setup.md:61`, `open_pr.md:99` and `triage.md:74` all correctly delegate to manifest
entries — and all three point *here* for the details, where the instruction is a raw `gh` write. The
file never mentions the write manifest.

## K4. `grade_gate` instructs a file write with no way to land it

See D7 — `:110` appends to `docs/agent-ledger.md`, but the phase has two steps and step 2 is Stop,
with no commit, no push, and no `push` manifest entry.

## K5. Two phases state opposite thread-resolution policy

`address_comments.md:29-33`: a disputed thread stays open, unconditionally — *"disputing and clearing
your own gate is not [fine]"*. `grade_gate.md:47-48`: for `auto-ok`, *"You may … resolve your own
threads … the gate trusts the self-resolution."* Same act, opposite rules, no cross-reference.
`grade_gate.md:49` gets `needs-review` right.

## K6. The risk-path gate row grades against the generic list, not this project's

`grade_gate.md:29` says *"The diff vs. `acceptance-criteria.md`'s risk list"* — that list
(`:122-125`) is the generic default. This repo's gated set is `CLAUDE.md`'s allowlist. **A run
grading itself against the generic list would report `risk-paths: none` on a `skills/**` diff.**

## K7. The skill knows only `CLAUDE.md`, never `AGENTS.md`

`acceptance-criteria.md:125`, `session-setup.md:19`, `github-projects.md:5,12,122,137,141`. A
Codex-hosted run reading `AGENTS.md` would find its own board config invisible to the skill.
`CLAUDE.md:41` already uses the neutral phrasing *"the project's instruction file"*.

## K8. `write-manifest.md` matched `writes.KINDS` exactly — ten kinds, ten matches

Recorded as a positive because it is the counter-example. Required/optional fields agree kind for
kind, no extras in either direction, no merge kind. Every documented behavioural rule checks out:
unknown kinds and unknown *fields* rejected (which is what pins every write to the driver's repo,
since `repo` is not an allowed field), all-or-nothing application, `push` refusing
`main`/`master`/`trunk` and never force-pushing, ordered execution stopping at first failure,
`$AGENT_SESSION_WRITES` matching `WRITES_FILE_VAR`. **The best-maintained document in the skill** —
the only one whose "read the code if we disagree" pointer is currently unnecessary. Two soft notes:
it omits `BOARD_KINDS`, so the "needs a board configured" rejection will surprise an agent that
records a project write on an unconfigured driver; and per K3, `github-projects.md` never learned it
exists.

## K9. Judgment calls for a human — not defects, decisions made in passing

- **The Ceremony Threshold has made the frozen-check contract optional in the case the docs call
  modal.** Escapes at `SKILL.md:82-88`, `plan.md:26`, `execute.md:37`, `open_pr.md:30`,
  `session-setup.md:57-58`, `frozen-checks.md:7` say small/tactical work skips `checks.md` and the
  freeze entirely. Then `execute.md:113-114`: *"Step 4's independent verification is not part of what
  you skip … **Most issues an unattended loop picks up are this size.**"* But the verifier's entire
  input is `checks.md` (`frozen-checks.md:161-163`), which the threshold just deleted.
  `grade_gate.md:17` half-acknowledges it (*"For small tasks without frozen checks, ignore the first
  four rows"*) — which means **the gate for most runs reduces to CI + threads + tier**, a materially
  weaker gate than the one the skill documents. Either define a minimum oracle for the small case, or
  say plainly that the frozen-check machinery is the exception rather than the rule.
- **On OpenCode, subagents are denied and nothing says so.** `agent_runner.py:118-121` sets
  `"task": "deny"` because *"OpenCode 1.18.18 does not propagate an agent's configured mandatory
  policy to delegated agents."* Subagents are the delivery mechanism for the check-author,
  check-reviewer, independent verifier, documentarians, and triage's fan-out. On that backend none can
  be dispatched, and no phase or reference states the fallback. `frozen-checks.md`'s 338 lines are
  earned in principle; the problem is that a supported backend cannot execute them and it is not
  written down.

---

# Governance

## G1. `AGENTS.md` should become a pointer to `CLAUDE.md`

`diff CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md` yields exactly four hunks. **The risk-gated section is byte-identical —
the parity check in `docs_check.py:302` is working.** Everything outside it drifted, which is the
argument:

| # | line | divergence | assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | `~/.claude/skills/` → `~/.Codex/skills/` | find-and-replace applied to a **filesystem path**. Resolves on this Mac only because APFS is case-insensitive; the capitalisation matches no real path. |
| 2 | 22 | `~/.claude/skills/dev-session/` → `~/.Codex/skills/dev-session/` | same, and **both directories exist as different copies**, so *"adapt from it; don't edit it"* names two different sources of truth depending on which file was read. |
| 3 | 177 | `claude -p` → `Codex -p` | **falsified flag.** Verified against the installed binary: there is no `-p`; non-interactive Codex is `codex exec`. |
| 4 | 205-209 | `AGENTS.md` **omits the world-state-claim rule entirely**, understates `docs-check` by one of its six checks, and says *"two real defects on its first run, one of which had survived two readings"* | genuine one-directional content drift, and hunk 4 carries the exact undated-count pattern `CLAUDE.md:205-207` forbids two lines earlier. |

Hunks 1–3 are facts about the filesystem and the CLI, not about the reader. **Recommendation: make
`AGENTS.md` one line pointing at `CLAUDE.md`.** The guarded section stayed in sync; the unguarded
remainder did not, and there is no bound on how much unguarded remainder there will be. Second
choice: widen the parity check to the whole file — mechanically sound, but it makes them
byte-identical, at which point the pointer is strictly cheaper. **Reject** keeping them in sync by
hand: that is what produced hunk 4.

## G2. `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` still place the detector tests at the repo root

`:109-111` — *"Its root-level test, `scripts/test_docs_check.py`, is drivable … their root-level
tests under `scripts/`"* — and `:115` *"root-level detector tests"*. Falsified by #257/#258. The
**Drivable** bullet at `:123` *was* updated to `tests/scripts/test_*.py`, so the same session that
fixed the bullet left the prose two paragraphs above it wrong — the "ask what it just invalidated"
failure shape, in the section that describes it. `docs_check.check_partition` misses it because it
inspects only the first backtick of **bullet** lines.

## G3. `docs_check`'s `is_shim` guard misses the live instance it was written for

`CLAUDE.md:74`/`AGENTS.md:74` gate `src/agent_sessions/driver/agent_session_driver.py` as *"the
current home of the outcome routing"* — false since #256; the routing is
`lifecycle.classify_and_record`. `check_partition`'s `is_shim` guard (`docs_check.py:224-235`) exists
precisely to catch a partition naming a re-export facade instead of the implementation, and it passes
here: the file has no `"Shim re-exporting"` marker and is 143 lines, over the 30-line threshold.

**The allowlist still holds** — unlisted `lifecycle.py` defaults to `needs-review`, so nothing is
exposed. But the gate's stated *reason* is now attached to a facade. Worth an issue against
`is_shim`, and worth a decision on whether `lifecycle.py` should be named explicitly.

---

issue.title: Review: full-repo maintainability and documentation audit (2026-08-19)

labels.name: needs-review
labels.description: A human-judgment criterion or a risk-gated path

issue.body:
## Context

Full-repo maintainability and documentation review, 2026-08-19. Seven parallel reviewers over the
driver core, the scripts package, the test suites, `design.md`/`orientation.md`/`README.md`,
`usage.md`/`findings.md`/`prior-art.md`, `skills/**` plus `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, and build/CI/repo
hygiene. Every claim below was re-verified against the code by hand before landing here; findings
that did not survive verification were dropped.

This issue is the capture record. Items are individually actionable and most want their own PR —
several touch risk-gated paths and cannot be batched with drivable work.

### The one pattern behind most of it

Six of seven reviewers independently found the same shape: **the 2026-08-09 Bash→Python conversion
and the #246/#257/#258 moves relabelled code without moving what pointed at it, and every loose end
fails green.** Six dangling `driver/`-relative paths, none of which turn anything red — an
`is_file()` guard silently skips, `testpaths` exits 0 having run nothing, `docs_check` prints an
honest SKIP that `make check` then ignores, `run_swarm` prints an error where nothing invokes it.

This is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` § *"When you change something, ask what it just invalidated"*
describes, arriving at scale. The structural reason it keeps landing undetected: **`docs_check` only
sees `[text](target)` markdown links, and the skill cites everything in backticks.** Three greps —
over backticked paths, mode names, and label names — would have caught eleven of the sixteen
falsified skill references below.

## Already fixed

On branch `chore/docs-archive-and-build-paths` (not yet PR'd):

- GitHub App private key moved out of the repo root to `~/.config/agent-session/`, `.env` repointed,
  and the `*.private-key.pem` ignore rule committed. It had existed only as an unstaged working-tree
  edit. The key was never committed — verified across every reachable git object.
- 26 pre-2026-08-09 dev-sessions archived to `docs/archive/dev-sessions/` via a new
  `scripts/archive-dev-session.py`. Tracked files under `docs/dev-sessions/` went 326 → 21.
- `pyproject.toml`: `testpaths` repaired (see S3), `pythonpath = ["src"]` added, dead ruff
  per-file-ignores removed, ruff `exclude` extended to `docs/archive`.

---

# Safety

## S1. The merge prohibition has no guard on the REST merge endpoint for the default backend

The complete effective Claude policy at the `Popen` boundary, printed from shipping code:

```
ALLOWED: Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Task,TodoWrite,BashOutput,KillShell,NotebookEdit,Bash(*)
DENIED : Bash(gh pr merge:*), Bash(gh pr merge *), Bash(git push --force:*),
         Bash(gh repo delete:*), Edit/Write/NotebookEdit(<skill_dir>/**)
```

`Bash(*)` is allowed and four patterns are denied. `gh api --method PUT /repos/o/r/pulls/N/merge`
and the `curl` equivalent are **not** among them. `OPENCODE_DENIED_COMMANDS`
(`src/agent_sessions/driver/agent_runner.py:62-63`) *does* deny both, so the non-default backend is
the better-defended one. `git push -f` (short form) is denied on neither — `BASE_DENIED_TOOLS`
spells only `git push --force`.

The only layer that ever covered those vectors is the PreToolUse hook — see S2.

**Fix:** add `gh api *pulls/*/merge*`, `curl *pulls/*/merge*`, and the `-f` short form to
`BASE_DENIED_TOOLS` so Claude's floor matches OpenCode's rather than depending on a hook.
**Tier:** `needs-review` — authorization work on a gated shipping path.

## S2. The PreToolUse merge-block hook has not been installed since the Python conversion

`src/agent_sessions/driver/lifecycle.py:374-375` resolves the hook assets next to itself:

```python
hook_settings_template = Path(__file__).parent / "settings.json"
hook_script = Path(__file__).parent / "merge-block-hook.sh"
```

`src/agent_sessions/driver/` contains only `.py` files; both assets live in repo-root `driver/` and
always have. So `hook_settings_template.is_file()` is False, `state_dir/settings.json` is never
written, and `lifecycle.py:930` passes `--settings <nonexistent path>` to the agent anyway.

## C4. The full-loop suite's lock-isolation is inert, and the leak fires real `git push` at exit

`tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:735-737`:

```python
# The driver releases its lock from an atexit hook keyed on this global.
# monkeypatch restores it to None, so no pass can leave a live lock behind.
monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE", None)
```

The comment is wrong. `agent_session_driver.py:48` does `from ...locks import CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE`,
binding a **copy** of a `str | None`; `locks.release_lock`/`acquire_lock` read and write
`locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` via `global`. Nothing in `src/` reads the re-exported name. Demonstrated:
patching the barrel leaves `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` untouched.

Observable on every suite run — these are the `atexit` hook firing at worker shutdown, *after*
monkeypatch has restored the real `subprocess.run`:

```
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #102...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #101...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #109...
```

Harmless today only because the `tmp_path` repos have no `origin`. A test that ever pointed
`--repo-path` at a real checkout would push a ref deletion to a real remote from a test process.

**Fix:** patch `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` (the owning module) or add `locks.reset()`; add an autouse
teardown asserting it is `None`; drop `CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` from the barrel's re-exports so nobody
re-derives the wrong seam. **Tier:** `auto-ok` for the test half.

# Structural

## T1. `agent_session_driver.py` is a re-export barrel that the package calls back through

143 lines that **define nothing** — an import list plus a 58-entry `__all__` and
`if __name__ == "__main__"`. Its `__all__` re-exports the standard library (`"datetime"`,
`"timezone"`) to serve **one line**: `tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:734` freezing time via
`monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "datetime", FrozenDatetime)`. To make that reachable,
`lifecycle.log()` and `locks.log()` each do a function-local import of the barrel purely to fetch
`agent_session_driver.datetime`.

`lifecycle.py` calls back through the barrel **44 times**, including `agent_session_driver.whoami` at
`:270` for a function defined at `lifecycle.py:146` — lifecycle calling itself via a module that
imports it. The cycle survives only because four modules defer their imports into function bodies
(14 sites across `lifecycle`, `board`, `parking`, `locks`). `board.say()` reaches the barrel, which
re-exports `lifecycle.say`, to write one line to stdout — while `lifecycle`, `parking` and
`pr_checks` define a **second, divergent** `say` that writes to stdout directly, so output behaviour
depends on which module you are in. Five spellings of one output helper set (four `say`, two `log`,
two `die`).

Read: **#246's decomposition is half-landed.** It extracted `RunContext` and named the lifecycle
operations, but kept the old god-module as a compatibility barrel so existing tests would not need
rewriting — and the modules now reach back through it. The seams were named without being cut. C4 is
the first concrete cost.

`agent_session_driver.py:14` also carries `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))`, a
pre-package fossil that puts the package directory on `sys.path`, making `board`, `locks`, `gate`,
`router`, `credentials` importable as top-level names. Nothing needs it.

**Fix, smallest first:** a tiny `driver/output.py` (`say`/`log`/`die`, no driver imports) that all
six modules import — this alone breaks three of `board.py`'s four barrel dependencies. Then move the
time seam to the owning module and delete the barrel's stdlib re-exports. Do **not** attempt full
de-shimming as unattended work. Distinct from #247, which is about the *GitHub I/O* surface; this is
the intra-package call graph. **Tier:** `needs-review` — gated file.

## T2. The lifecycle operations were named but not decomposed

`invoke_agent` 286 lines, `preflight` 230, `classify_and_record` 186, `select_queue` 162; and
`router.select` is a single 222-line function. The four-function shape from #246 is sound and I am
not proposing more than two extractions, each with an obvious seam:

  the recovery instruction three times.
- **`locks.py:120-152`'s stale-lock steal and TTL are untested.** No test references
  `force-with-lease`, `ttl`, or the steal path. Untested: `lock_age >= ttl_seconds` → force-with-lease
  push; the 600s/7200s split by phase (`locks.py:71`); a lease that *loses* the race; `release_lock`
  itself. This is the distributed mutual-exclusion primitive — get the TTL wrong and two drivers run
  the same issue, spending budget twice. `FakeGitHub.held_locks` already takes a timestamp, so the
  steal case is a one-line fixture change.

## X5. Slow, fragile, and CWD-dependent tests

- **One test is 85% of the wall clock.** `test_gate_test_wiring.py::test_new_test_file_runs_under_gate_test_with_no_makefile_edit`
  takes 30.3s of a 35.6s run because it invokes `make gate-test` twice for real — so `make check`
  runs the whole suite three times over. **Do not weaken it**; it is the only thing standing between
  you and a test file that silently never runs. Worth knowing the floor is ~3×, and worth an `-x` on
  the with-probe arm, which only needs to observe one failure.
- `xdist_group` at `test_gate_test_wiring.py:44` is **inert** — it is honoured only under
  `--dist loadgroup`, and `make gate-test` runs `-n auto` with no `--dist`. C1 and C2 can land on
  different workers and run concurrently while C2 writes a probe file into the tree C1 is collecting.
  Masked today by the process-unique probe name.
- No git-config isolation in any `git init` fixture: no `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, no
  `commit.gpgsign=false`. A developer or CI image with global `commit.gpgsign` or `core.hooksPath`
  breaks eight tests in a way that reads as a code failure.
- CWD-relative paths in `test_driver_settings.py:8,10,15,23,24`, `test_merge_hook.py:7,13,19,25,30`,
  `test_board_audit.py:443,563`, `test_gate.py:222,551`, while every other suite derives
  `parents[2]`. `test_driver_settings.py:9-10` silently falls back to a *different* file if
  `lifecycle.py` is missing, so a rename makes it grade the wrong artifact rather than fail. It also
  requires `jq` on `$PATH`.
- `test_evidence.py:27,40,46` replaces `builtins.open` and `Path.is_file` process-wide;
  `test_discussion_manager.py:16-17` builds expected titles from the real wall clock, so crossing UTC
  midnight between two calls fails the test.
- Vacuous: `test_writes.py:93` (`assert spec is not None` over `KINDS.items()`),
  `test_driver.py:527` (`isinstance(..., list)` immediately before a length assertion),
  `test_docs_check.py:36,52` (defensive `getattr` then `assert ... is not None`).

**On `test_full_loop.py`: I would argue against splitting it.** 1594 lines, but one harness, one
fake, one stub agent, and five explicitly labelled case groups whose seam is *the driver pass*, not a
module. Its assertions are whole-object equality on `runs.jsonl` rows and whole-list equality on
`label_ops`, and `LoopHarness.run` asserts `gh.unhandled == []` and `gh.field_gaps == []` on every
pass. Extract the harness to `conftest.py`; leave the bodies together.

---

comment.body:
> Continued from the issue body — full-repo review, 2026-08-19.

# Documentation

## D1. `usage.md` — the worst-rotted document, and the one where it costs most

Two defects are the ones an operator reaches for under pressure:

- **`:328`, `:356` name `driver-parked`.** The label is `agent-session:needs-human`
  (`parking.py:13`). `driver-parked` exists nowhere in `src/` — it survives only in the session that
  *proposed* it, plus as a stale label still present in the repo. `:356` explicitly instructs the
  manual recovery action (*"you take the label off by hand"*), making this the wrong string most
  likely to be acted on. The second park label,
  `agent-session:needs-human-interactive`, is undocumented and equally load-bearing.
- **`:345-352` has the Outcomes table inverted for two of nine rows.** It says `gate-human` → not
  parked and `incomplete` → parked. `parking.py:355-367`: `gate-human` calls `park_label_add`;
  `incomplete` says *"leaving unparked so the loop can re-evaluate later"* and calls
  `park_label_remove`. `:356`'s claim that reaching `gate-human` *removes* the label is falsified by
  the same code.

Also provably wrong:
- `:132` *"runs `express` on them unattended"* — `express` appears nowhere in `lifecycle.py`.
  `PHASE_TIERS` (`:27-36`) holds eight phases and the driver invokes **one phase per selection**.
  Part 4's whole "one run = one express pass" mental model is built on this.
- `:38`, `:107` describe a `pr` mode. It split into `open_pr` (opens with a **pending** verdict) and
  `grade_gate` (derives it later). `refine`, `rethink`, `fix_ci`, `fix_conflict`,
  `address_comments` are undocumented.
- `:327-337` "What eligible means" describes a superseded algorithm, including one condition now
  **inverted**: `:335` says the board column is *"advisory — reported but doesn't gate"*, while
  `router.py:66-77` filters to `Ready` or a `P0`–`P5` label unless `--all-issues`. Also: an open PR
  is now the *highest* priority (`p1_unblock`), not an exclusion; `needs-review` is selectable via
  `refine`; eligibility is a label or the marker. The P1–P4 ladder and attempt-count parking are
  undocumented, and `MAX_PHASE_ATTEMPTS (3) reached for phase {phase}` is a park reason an operator
  will see and cannot look up.
- `:156` vs `:181` **contradict each other** on where the write token lives — the table says *"your
  shell, never `.env`"*, the prose 25 lines later says *"Both go in `.env`"* and dates the decision
  to 2026-08-10. `.env.example` and `credentials.py:29-30` side with the prose.
- `:226` *"no third option short of a GitHub App"* and `:317` *"None of these is built"* — GitHub App
  auth **is** implemented: `credentials.py:41-43` (three vars plus `GH_APP_*` aliases), `:130`
  `generate_app_jwt`, `:158` `fetch_app_installation_token`, minting scoped read and write
  installation tokens separately. Knock-ons: `:163` *"All three are required and there is no
  fallback"* is false with App vars set, and `DRIVER_GH_BOARD_TOKEN` (`credentials.py:33`) — the
  documented answer to the board-scope problem at `:263-266` — is mentioned nowhere.
- `:419` lists a `denials.txt` per-run artifact that is **never written**. Undocumented and
  operator-relevant: `stderr.txt` (the first thing you want on a `driver-fault`), `parsed.json`, and
  `inbox.md` in the state dir — the human work queue that `parking.notify_human` appends to.
- `:445` *"A run leaves a worktree in the repo root"* — workspace isolation is on by default and
  worktrees land under `<state-dir>/workspaces/`. The **advice is still right**; the reason no longer
  holds, and a reader who checks the reason discounts the advice.

**Organisationally:** 178 of Part 4's ~300 lines are a credentials essay that states the
fine-grained-PAT resource-owner rule three times (`:214`, `:221`, `:251`) and carries two tables over
the same taxonomy (`:208-213`, `:246-249`), while setup (`scripts/bootstrap-repo.sh`) is never
mentioned anywhere and **watching a run is absent entirely** — no `make watch`/`watch-self`, no
`make evidence`, no mention of the Lab Notebook discussion that `lifecycle.py:848,1137` posts to on
every run. The Makefile's own comment for `watch` diagnoses the operator problem the guide should be
solving: *"a run is a black box for as long as it lasts."* Parts 1–3 are still substantially accurate
and are the best prose in the repo.

**Recommendation:** patch the label, the Outcomes table, and the token contradiction **today** —
three one-line fixes that prevent wrong actions. Then lift `:179-324` into `docs/credentials.md` and
rewrite Part 4 as configure → dry-run → run → watch → outcomes → when it dies.

## D2. `design.md` — the roadmap rot came back, and it is cited as the precedent

`:389-407` opens ***"The backlog is not maintained here any more."*** and then reproduces an 8-row
issue table. Verified: #1, #2, #5, #6, #7, #12, #13 are **CLOSED**; only #3 is open. `CLAUDE.md`'s
documentation section cites this exact section as the precedent (*"`design.md`'s roadmap duplicated
the board and rotted within two days"*). **Deleting the table is the highest-value single edit in the
audit**; the link on `:391` is sufficient.

Also:
- `:265-273` inventories the coordinator as *"`agent_session_driver.py` — the coordinator:
  configuration, credentials, GitHub reads, workspaces, agent invocation, outcome routing,
  persistence, and reporting."* That file is now a 143-line facade. `lifecycle.py` — the largest
  module in the repo — is mentioned in **none** of `design.md`, `orientation.md`, `README.md`, or
  `archive/README.md`. The list also names 4 of 16 modules.
- `:490` attributes verdict derivation to `pr.md`; `:305` correctly says `grade_gate`, 185 lines
  earlier.
- `:605` names `driver-parked` (renamed by Epic #145).
- `:340` documents a **P4 priority that is never populated** (T4); `:339` omits that P3 also carries
  every specced `needs-review` issue, routed to `refine`.
- `:348-352` "Stateless Resumption" says an unparked issue re-enters at P3/`triage`. Only markerless
  issues go there; an unparked specced `auto-ok` issue with no PR goes to P2/`execute`, one with an
  open PR to P1.
- `:448` cites `plan.md:84` for a rule now at `plan.md:92` — drop the line number, keep the
  greppable quote.
- `:328` says `merge-ready` awaits *"human merge or auto-merger"*; auto-merge is explicitly not
  pursued (`:138`, `:472`).
- **Structure:** at 655 lines it is a layered accretion whose own headings admit it — `:143` *"the
  original sketch — architecture superseded"*, `:415` *"The open decision (Superseded)"*, and `:450`
  *"Dropped in this reconciliation"*, a one-time move-7 bookkeeping artifact. Its *reasoning*
  sections (the one principle, front-loading, criteria vs. guards, Resolved decisions) are genuinely
  durable and are the document's value. Moving `:389-466` to
  `docs/archive/design-reconciliation-move7.md`, deleting the `:265-312` inventory in favour of a
  pointer to `orientation.md`, and deleting `:369-388` is ~−180 lines with no loss of reasoning.

## D3. `orientation.md` — the best of the four, and it should absorb the inventory role

Its glossary (`:69-86`), seams table (`:208-222`) and subagent-cast table (`:229-245`) exist nowhere
else and are the only written record of the system's text-format contracts. **Keep it.** Its defects
are almost entirely in file-inventory rows — exactly the content that should be cited rather than
typed:
- `:114`, `:116`, `:176`, `:185`, `:190`, `:194-195`, `:373` still place the harness tests at
  `driver/test_*.py` and `scripts/test_*.py`. `driver/` now holds three files, `scripts/` one.
- `:180`, `:84` repeat D2's coordinator claim.
- `:372-374` restates the risk partition and **omits `tests/**`**. This is prose restating a live
  source, which `CLAUDE.md` forbids; `docs_check` enforces CLAUDE/AGENTS parity but not either
  against `orientation.md`. **Delete the restatement**; the pointer in the same paragraph suffices.
- `:97-100` says the harness is *"only this repo"* while `design.md:246` says *"target repositories
  and CI environments"*. Design is right (`Makefile:3-5` defaults to decafclaw; the ledger shows 292
  decafclaw runs).
- `:296-308` describes the driver as a four-step express-only loop; selection has four branches and
  `request_review` runs deterministically with no agent at all (`lifecycle.py:858-864`).
- `:136`, `:139`, `:157`, `:285` reference `phases/pr.md`.

## D4. `README.md`

First paragraph is accurate and needs no change. `:49` attributes the merge gate to *"the harness
(`driver/` + `Makefile`)"* — the harness is `src/agent_sessions/`, and it inverts the documented
ownership: `design.md:520` and `orientation.md:303-306` both say the driver **reads** the gate block
rather than re-deriving it, *"so the skill owns the verdict and the driver owns only the routing."*
`:57` says *"Six modes"* (`SKILL.md` lists ten; twelve phase files exist). `:156-159` documents a
`/agent-session intake` slash command while `orientation.md:106` says the skill is **not installed** —
verified, it isn't. `:168` files `make check` under "Run the driver over a board" when it is the full
aggregate. `:212` link text says `docs/build-log.md`, href says `docs/archive/build-log.md`.
`:190-192` carries three uncited world-state claims, the last phrased to evade `docs_check`'s
literal-number pattern.

## D5. `findings.md` — healthiest of the five; the citations rotted, not the reasoning

- **Five dead paths, two of which are runnable commands that fail:** `:115` (`driver/gate.py`),
  `:336` (`python3 scripts/commit_lint.py --all`), `:390` (`scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py`),
  `:479` (`driver/test-*.sh` — a file class the conversion deleted entirely, so the rule it supports
  silently covers half of what it claims), `:1032` (`python3 scripts/session_artifact_stats.py`).
- **Six references to `phases/pr.md` with step numbers** (`:457`, `:494`, `:531`, `:546`, `:806`,
  `:901`). Worse than a moved path: the split renumbered the steps, so these cannot be repaired by
  find-and-replace and need re-locating by hand.
- **The counts at the front misbehave in exactly the way the file itself warns about.** `:21` says
  *"Seven patterns"* over eight `### n.` sections. `:30` says *"Nine of the eleven below are fixed;
  two are open"* over a **twelve**-row table. Both "open" items are closed: #2 (*"Sweep every gate
  row…"*) and #79. So `:23`'s **OPEN GAP** header and `:36`'s bolded *"The sweep that has never been
  done"* are both false — and #2's output is checked into `docs/`. The file's own `:118` says *"which
  is why status now lives in the table's own column and not in a sentence above it"*, and `:30` is a
  sentence above it carrying status. Note `:649`'s *"Nine micro-test studies"* directly above its
  nine-row table is exactly right by `CLAUDE.md`'s rule and should be left alone.
- `:788`'s `createDiscussionCategory` gotcha: the **API fact is still true** (re-verified against the
  live GraphQL schema today), but the attached claim that `ensure_category` *"has been calling it
  since it was written, failing every time"* is stale — `discussion_manager.py:76-78` now delegates
  to `check_category`, and #211 is closed.
- `:1074-1080` duplicates `CLAUDE.md:215-224`'s "ask what it just invalidated" anecdote, and the
  findings.md copy is the un-maintained one (CLAUDE.md got the `src/` path update). **CLAUDE.md
  should be canonical** here. Conversely `:218`'s "3 for 3" and `CLAUDE.md:211` state the same fact,
  and **findings.md should be canonical** there — it has the adjacent table that makes the count
  countable.
- **~250 lines are now history** and would lose nothing in `docs/archive/`: the seven-instance
  verifier narrative (`:573-648`), the instrument rules (`:707-740`, scoped to a research programme
  `:682-706` declares too expensive to continue), and most of "Operational figures" (`:870-1051`) —
  keeping the durable residue of each: the cost range, in-flight spend being unobservable, and "drive
  long runs from a terminal."

**The command gotchas re-verified well.** Against installed gh 2.96.0, Claude Code 2.1.236, OpenCode
1.18.18, pytest 9.1.1: of 33 gotchas, **1 is affirmatively no longer true as written** — `:25`, `gh`
writes posting as the repo owner, superseded by the #191 credential split (the *conclusion* still
holds for a different reason: the machine user is still not a human, and `credentials.py:57`
documents the new hazard, that a PAT-backed account has no `[bot]` suffix — #183). One carries a
stale codebase claim on a true API fact (`:31`, above), one has an unreachable precondition today
(`:17`, `--required` — both target repos now *have* required checks, so the exit-1 trap can't be
reproduced; the advice to grade all checks is unaffected), and one has a **fired-but-unactioned
conditional**: `:10` says *"if that hook lands, teach the denial detector about it"* — the hook
landed. The remaining 29 re-verified true or are unverifiable without a write with nothing
contradicting them. **Nothing in the gotchas will lead you into a wrong flag list**, which is what
`CLAUDE.md` invokes them for. Caveat worth recording: all four OpenCode rows are pinned to 1.18.18
*and* the installed binary is 1.18.18, so they are simultaneously maximally trustworthy and maximally
fragile — the first upgrade invalidates all four at once with no detector watching.

## D6. `sweep-adjacent-evidence.md` — archive it

It is #2's output, referenced from exactly one line (`findings.md:56`). It reports
`adjacent-risk: none` for **all 26 rows** — including `threads`, which `findings.md:56` documents at
length as the canonical adjacency instance, and `project-gates`, which `prior-art.md:235`
independently nominates as another. It reads its conditions out of a `phases/pr.md` that no longer
exists (`:19`) and lists a Makefile check set predating `lint` and `typecheck` (`:38-44`). A sweep
whose purpose was asking *"what could satisfy this that is not the thing it names?"* and that answers
"nothing, 26 times" against a corpus containing two known instances is a vacuous check in a file —
**defect class 6, in the document that defines defect class 6.** Archive rather than delete: the
useful finding is that the sweep was run and produced nothing, and archiving lets `findings.md`'s
OPEN GAP header become honest rather than closed-on-paper.

## D7. `agent-ledger.md` — live, not vestigial, and its emptiness is a harness finding

`skills/agent-session/phases/intake.md:9` **reads** it; `phases/grade_gate.md:110` **writes** it on
every `eligible-for-auto-merge` verdict. The ledger shows eleven such verdicts across two repos. The
file still says *"(Initial placeholder)"*. So the append has never fired, and the likely mechanism is
structural: it is a local doc write inside the run's workspace that would have to ride along in a PR
scoped to something else — and `grade_gate` has no commit, no push, and no `push` manifest entry
(`:120` is Stop). **Keep the file** (deleting it silently changes `intake`'s inputs); **fix the
harness.** Either record a `push`, or move the ledger append into `open_pr` before its push.

## D8. `prior-art.md` — best-aged; two one-line fixes

All 27 external links resolve 200. Its `[unverified]` discipline and willingness to strike its own
claims in place are why it aged well. Two defects: `:198` says a revision-first queue policy is *"a
queue policy our driver does not have and probably needs"* — `router.py:158-181`'s P1 Unblock ladder
**is** that policy, a textbook self-invalidated claim; and `:225` *"eight PRs deep with nothing
merged is where the field is, not where this project is behind"* reads as current standing when the
count is 138 merged as of 2026-08-19. Per `CLAUDE.md`, inline the date rather than update the number.

## D9. Missing documentation (all three real)

1. **The `refine` phase.** Every specced `needs-review` issue routes to it (`router.py:187-197`); it
   has its own park semantics (#255). It appears in **no** document. A newcomer would conclude
   `needs-review` issues are simply skipped.
2. **`agent_runner.py` and the backend permission policy.** 603 lines, in no document, yet
   `README.md:49` advertises *"pluggable agent backends"* and `Makefile:83-87` makes three of its
   tests the entire `skill-readonly` guard. It is the mechanism behind "nothing merges by machine"
   and cannot be inferred.
3. **Where `main()` lives.** Nothing tells a contributor the run lifecycle is `lifecycle.py` and that
   `agent_session_driver.py` is a facade kept for `[project.scripts]`. The single most likely thing to
   send someone to the wrong file.

issue.title: Review: full-repo maintainability and documentation audit (2026-08-19)

labels.description: A human-judgment criterion or a risk-gated path

issue.body:
## Context

Full-repo maintainability and documentation review, 2026-08-19. Seven parallel reviewers over the
driver core, the scripts package, the test suites, `design.md`/`orientation.md`/`README.md`,
`usage.md`/`findings.md`/`prior-art.md`, `skills/**` plus `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, and build/CI/repo
hygiene. Every claim below was re-verified against the code by hand before landing here; findings
that did not survive verification were dropped.

This issue is the capture record. Items are individually actionable and most want their own PR —
several touch risk-gated paths and cannot be batched with drivable work.

### The one pattern behind most of it

Six of seven reviewers independently found the same shape: **the 2026-08-09 Bash→Python conversion
and the #246/#257/#258 moves relabelled code without moving what pointed at it, and every loose end
fails green.** Six dangling `driver/`-relative paths, none of which turn anything red — an
`is_file()` guard silently skips, `testpaths` exits 0 having run nothing, `docs_check` prints an
honest SKIP that `make check` then ignores, `run_swarm` prints an error where nothing invokes it.

This is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` § *"When you change something, ask what it just invalidated"*
describes, arriving at scale. The structural reason it keeps landing undetected: **`docs_check` only
sees `[text](target)` markdown links, and the skill cites everything in backticks.** Three greps —
over backticked paths, mode names, and label names — would have caught eleven of the sixteen
falsified skill references below.

## Already fixed

On branch `chore/docs-archive-and-build-paths` (not yet PR'd):

- GitHub App private key moved out of the repo root to `~/.config/agent-session/`, `.env` repointed,
  and the `*.private-key.pem` ignore rule committed. It had existed only as an unstaged working-tree
  edit. The key was never committed — verified across every reachable git object.
- 26 pre-2026-08-09 dev-sessions archived to `docs/archive/dev-sessions/` via a new
  `scripts/archive-dev-session.py`. Tracked files under `docs/dev-sessions/` went 326 → 21.
- `pyproject.toml`: `testpaths` repaired (see S3), `pythonpath = ["src"]` added, dead ruff
  per-file-ignores removed, ruff `exclude` extended to `docs/archive`.

---

# Safety

## S1. The merge prohibition has no guard on the REST merge endpoint for the default backend

The complete effective Claude policy at the `Popen` boundary, printed from shipping code:

```
ALLOWED: Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Task,TodoWrite,BashOutput,KillShell,NotebookEdit,Bash(*)
DENIED : Bash(gh pr merge:*), Bash(gh pr merge *), Bash(git push --force:*),
         Bash(gh repo delete:*), Edit/Write/NotebookEdit(<skill_dir>/**)
```

`Bash(*)` is allowed and four patterns are denied. `gh api --method PUT /repos/o/r/pulls/N/merge`
and the `curl` equivalent are **not** among them. `OPENCODE_DENIED_COMMANDS`
(`src/agent_sessions/driver/agent_runner.py:62-63`) *does* deny both, so the non-default backend is
the better-defended one. `git push -f` (short form) is denied on neither — `BASE_DENIED_TOOLS`
spells only `git push --force`.

The only layer that ever covered those vectors is the PreToolUse hook — see S2.

**Fix:** add `gh api *pulls/*/merge*`, `curl *pulls/*/merge*`, and the `-f` short form to
`BASE_DENIED_TOOLS` so Claude's floor matches OpenCode's rather than depending on a hook.
**Tier:** `needs-review` — authorization work on a gated shipping path.

## S2. The PreToolUse merge-block hook has not been installed since the Python conversion

`src/agent_sessions/driver/lifecycle.py:374-375` resolves the hook assets next to itself:

```python
hook_settings_template = Path(__file__).parent / "settings.json"
hook_script = Path(__file__).parent / "merge-block-hook.sh"
```

`src/agent_sessions/driver/` contains only `.py` files; both assets live in repo-root `driver/` and
always have. So `hook_settings_template.is_file()` is False, `state_dir/settings.json` is never
written, and `lifecycle.py:930` passes `--settings <nonexistent path>` to the agent anyway.
`src/agent_sessions/scripts/backend_permission_probe.py:37-38` resolves the same two files
correctly via `PROJECT_ROOT / "driver"`, which is what makes this an oversight rather than a
decision.

Evidence it has been off since 2026-08-09: this repo's `.driver-state/settings.json` is dated Aug 6
— a pre-conversion leftover that happens to point at a real script, which is why nothing has been
observed to break locally. The decafclaw state dir's copy points at
`.worktrees/issue-170/driver/merge-block-hook.sh`, a worktree that no longer exists.

Why no test caught it:
- `tests/driver/test_driver_settings.py:12` asserts the string `--settings` appears in
  `lifecycle.py`'s **source text** — a presence-grep in Python clothing, satisfied by a comment.
  `assertion-lint` cannot see it because it matches only `grep -q`.
- `tests/driver/test_driver_settings.py:26-33` shells out to `jq` and asserts that **jq's assignment
  operator works**. The shipping code renders with `json.loads`/`dumps`. Nothing here calls
  `preflight`.
- `tests/driver/test_merge_hook.py:7` runs the launcher's copy of the script, not the path the
  shipping code resolves.
- `make driver-check` greps only the 8-line compatibility launcher (already tracked by #248).

**Fix:** move the two assets into the package (and ship them as package data), or point
`lifecycle.py` at `PROJECT_ROOT / "driver"` to match the probe. Then **drop the `if ... is_file()`
guard or make the miss loud** — a safety control that silently skips itself when its asset is
missing is the bug behind the bug. Replace the two tests with one that calls `preflight` and asserts
the rendered settings file exists and its `command` points at an executable file.
**Tier:** `needs-review` — gated coordinator, and it is a safety boundary.

## S3. A bare `pytest` reported success having run nothing *(fixed, recorded for the class)*

`pyproject.toml` still read `testpaths = ["driver", "scripts"]` after #257/#258 moved the suites;
both directories now hold only shell assets. `uv run pytest` collected zero tests and **exited 0**.
`make gate-test` passes explicit globs, so CI stayed honest and only the default was a false green.

Fixed on the branch above. Recorded because the class is the point: the relocation commits did not
carry `pyproject.toml`, and no check compares the two. **A guard asserting that a bare `pytest`
collects a non-zero count would close it** — `tests/scripts/test_gate_test_wiring.py` already does

## C4. The full-loop suite's lock-isolation is inert, and the leak fires real `git push` at exit

`tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:735-737`:

```python
# The driver releases its lock from an atexit hook keyed on this global.
# monkeypatch restores it to None, so no pass can leave a live lock behind.
monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE", None)
```

The comment is wrong. `agent_session_driver.py:48` does `from ...locks import CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE`,
binding a **copy** of a `str | None`; `locks.release_lock`/`acquire_lock` read and write
`locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` via `global`. Nothing in `src/` reads the re-exported name. Demonstrated:
patching the barrel leaves `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` untouched.

Observable on every suite run — these are the `atexit` hook firing at worker shutdown, *after*
monkeypatch has restored the real `subprocess.run`:

```
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #102...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #101...
22:00:34Z  Releasing lock for #109...
```

Harmless today only because the `tmp_path` repos have no `origin`. A test that ever pointed
`--repo-path` at a real checkout would push a ref deletion to a real remote from a test process.

**Fix:** patch `locks.CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` (the owning module) or add `locks.reset()`; add an autouse
teardown asserting it is `None`; drop `CURRENT_LOCK_ISSUE` from the barrel's re-exports so nobody
re-derives the wrong seam. **Tier:** `auto-ok` for the test half.

# Structural

## T1. `agent_session_driver.py` is a re-export barrel that the package calls back through

143 lines that **define nothing** — an import list plus a 58-entry `__all__` and
`if __name__ == "__main__"`. Its `__all__` re-exports the standard library (`"datetime"`,
`"timezone"`) to serve **one line**: `tests/driver/test_full_loop.py:734` freezing time via
`monkeypatch.setattr(agent_session_driver, "datetime", FrozenDatetime)`. To make that reachable,
`lifecycle.log()` and `locks.log()` each do a function-local import of the barrel purely to fetch
`agent_session_driver.datetime`.

`lifecycle.py` calls back through the barrel **44 times**, including `agent_session_driver.whoami` at
`:270` for a function defined at `lifecycle.py:146` — lifecycle calling itself via a module that
imports it. The cycle survives only because four modules defer their imports into function bodies
(14 sites across `lifecycle`, `board`, `parking`, `locks`). `board.say()` reaches the barrel, which
re-exports `lifecycle.say`, to write one line to stdout — while `lifecycle`, `parking` and
`pr_checks` define a **second, divergent** `say` that writes to stdout directly, so output behaviour
depends on which module you are in. Five spellings of one output helper set (four `say`, two `log`,
two `die`).

Read: **#246's decomposition is half-landed.** It extracted `RunContext` and named the lifecycle
operations, but kept the old god-module as a compatibility barrel so existing tests would not need
rewriting — and the modules now reach back through it. The seams were named without being cut. C4 is
the first concrete cost.

`agent_session_driver.py:14` also carries `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))`, a
pre-package fossil that puts the package directory on `sys.path`, making `board`, `locks`, `gate`,
`router`, `credentials` importable as top-level names. Nothing needs it.

**Fix, smallest first:** a tiny `driver/output.py` (`say`/`log`/`die`, no driver imports) that all
six modules import — this alone breaks three of `board.py`'s four barrel dependencies. Then move the
time seam to the owning module and delete the barrel's stdlib re-exports. Do **not** attempt full
de-shimming as unattended work. Distinct from #247, which is about the *GitHub I/O* surface; this is
the intra-package call graph. **Tier:** `needs-review` — gated file.

`invoke_agent` 286 lines, `preflight` 230, `classify_and_record` 186, `select_queue` 162; and
`router.select` is a single 222-line function. The four-function shape from #246 is sound and I am

  `test_discussion_manager.py:16-17` builds expected titles from the real wall clock, so crossing UTC
  midnight between two calls fails the test.
- Vacuous: `test_writes.py:93` (`assert spec is not None` over `KINDS.items()`),
  `test_driver.py:527` (`isinstance(..., list)` immediately before a length assertion),
  `test_docs_check.py:36,52` (defensive `getattr` then `assert ... is not None`).

**On `test_full_loop.py`: I would argue against splitting it.** 1594 lines, but one harness, one
fake, one stub agent, and five explicitly labelled case groups whose seam is *the driver pass*, not a
module. Its assertions are whole-object equality on `runs.jsonl` rows and whole-list equality on
`label_ops`, and `LoopHarness.run` asserts `gh.unhandled == []` and `gh.field_gaps == []` on every
pass. Extract the harness to `conftest.py`; leave the bodies together.

---
